papers.summary: We investigate $Z$-boson production in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$ within the $k_t$-factorization framework, using four nuclear transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution (TMD) prescriptions, namely LO-MRW, VO-MRW, MVO-MRW, and MKMRW. The aim of this study is to examine how different ordering conditions and normalization treatments influence the theoretical description of this process. We calculate the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions using the parton-level KaTie event generator and compare the predictions with CMS measurements and collinear NLO calculations. This comparison allows us to assess the sensitivity of the predicted distributions to the choice of UPDF prescription.

papers.title: Perturbative unitarity bounds from qubit entanglement in scalar scattering and QED
papers.summary: In the framework of $2\to 2$ relativistic scattering described by the perturbative $S$-matrix, we perform a comprehensive analysis of the properties of quantum channels obtained by tracing out the momentum from the scattered state. We work in two distinct scenarios with qubit degrees of freedom: flavored scalar contact interactions and QED, focusing in particular on initial-state leptons with transverse polarization. We identify the conditions that make the quantum channel unitary, calculate the entanglement of the qubits through the concurrence, and use its maximally allowed value to extract perturbativity upper bounds on the coupling constants. We find that the limits are often more constraining than the corresponding partial-wave expansion bounds, and that they allow us to bypass some of the obstacles associated in the latter with the singular behavior of forward scattering.

papers.title: Recipe for near-unity efficient frequency conversion via transient molecular modulation
papers.summary: Frequency transduction technologies are an essential element for interfacing devices operating at distinct spectral regions. Specifically, the conversion of weak signals between different wavelengths is a fundamental requirement of quantum networks, where conversion efficiency is critical for preserving the statistical properties of light. In this regard, molecular modulation in gas-filled hollow-core fibers offers a promising approach for highly-tunable linear frequency conversion of classical and quantum light. However, recent experimental studies in this subject have struggled to overcome a saturation in conversion efficiency to about 70%, which, although high, might impair the faithful transfer of quantum properties upon conversion. In this work, we discuss a route to surpass this limitation that identifies the key factors to consider for obtaining quantum efficiencies exceeding 99%. These results might pave the way to viable fiber-based quantum transduction schemes for next-generation quantum networks.

papers.title: An uncalibrated effective-one-body waveform model for intermediate-mass-ratio black hole binaries
papers.summary: Intermediate-mass-ratio binaries, with mass ratios $q=m_1/m_2\sim10^2-10^4$, are among the most challenging sources for waveform modeling. We present an inspiral-merger-ringdown effective-one-body model for nonspinning, quasicircular binaries with $q>10$, with dynamics built only from analytical post-Newtonian results. It reaches $(2,2)$ unfaithfulness of $10^{-4}-10^{-5}$ against numerical-relativity simulations with $q>10$ and subradian dephasing against second-order self-force waveforms over four-year inspirals at $q=10^4-10^5$. An optimized post-adiabatic implementation enables waveform generation up to two orders of magnitude faster than integrating the full equations of motion.
papers.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables, plus 3 pages of Supplemental Material (1 figure, 2 tables)

papers.title: Cosmological Constant Screening from Quantum Horizon Chaos
papers.summary: We propose a microscopic mechanism for screening the cosmological constant through quantum chaos of the horizon degrees of freedom. We show that in a recently proposed quantum-horizon matrix model arXiv:2406.01466, the Schwarzschild--de Sitter junction completion arXiv:2608.21178 supports a gravitationally dressed soft mode that approaches the massless minimally coupled scalar of de Sitter gravity. Interactions among the microscopic horizon degrees of freedom provide a mechanism for force relaxation. Assuming a finite-memory force spectrum with nonzero regular low-frequency weight, the gravitationally dressed soft mode undergoes Brownian diffusion after momentum relaxation. The resulting bosonic coarse-grained entropy supplements the background entropy arising from fermionic parton microstates. We propose that their sum defines the total thermodynamic entropy, which can be identified with the Gibbons--Hawking entropy of the backreacted causal horizon. Entropy generation during the diffusion regime then leads to infrared screening of the effective cosmological constant, with a universal entropy--variance coefficient agreeing with that of Kitazawa and collaborators. Radiative lifting of the soft mode provides a possible mechanism for terminating the screening regime.

papers.title: Snap-Through Symmetry Breaking in Multicellular Aggregates
papers.summary: Symmetry breaking is a fundamental process in biological organization. Yet the physical mechanisms that control its onset in multicellular systems remain poorly understood. Motivated by gastruloids -- multicellular aggregates in which cells differentiate and spontaneously break symmetry -- we study a two-phase viscoelastic solid drop as a minimal model of tissue polarization. We show that elastocapillary competition fundamentally alters the classical engulfing transition of fluid drops. While symmetry breaking occurs continuously in the purely viscous limit, bulk elasticity instead leads to a discontinuous snap-like transition. We demonstrate that this behavior can be understood as a wetting transition governed by a spreading coefficient which depends on the drop size and phase volume fraction. Applying our model to gastruloids, we find a critical volume fraction for symmetry breaking, providing a self-organized mechanism for robust developmental timing. Our results identify a generic elastocapillary transition that enables spontaneous symmetry breaking in biphasic drops.

papers.title: CORALIE Radial Velocity Search for Companions around Evolved Stars (CASCADES) VI. Revised masses and homogeneous estimation of the stellar parameters of 583 red giants
papers.summary: Giant-star radial-velocity surveys allow us to study how the exoplanet population varies with stellar mass and evolution. However, obtaining accurate estimates of stellar masses for such stars is challenging, as methods like isochrone fitting are prone to large errors due to the degeneracy associated with the closeness of isochrones. We provide a homogeneous re-derivation of the stellar parameters of the CASCADES giant-star survey. This includes parameters obtained from spectral energy distribution fitting, as well as an update of the stellar masses using asteroseismology. We use TESS light curves to measure the frequency of maximum oscillation power, $ν_{\rm max}$, for all the stars when applicable. We re-extract the stellar radii of the survey by fitting broadband photometry with ARIADNE, a spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting package, using priors from spectroscopy for the effective temperature, metallicity and $\log g$. By using scaling relations, we compute revised estimates of the stellar masses of targets with a $ν_{\rm max}$ measurement. We obtain new estimates of mass for 583 out of the 640 stars of the survey. These revised masses are typically 15 to 20% lower (median difference of $-0.35\,M_\odot$) than the ones obtained by isochrone fitting, in particular for low-metallicity stars for which this effect is stronger. These new masses impact the overall mass distribution of the sample, whose median decreases from $2.11\,M_\odot$ to $1.65\,M_\odot$. These revised masses provide the basis for future occurrence-rate analyses aiming to study the link between host-star mass and planet occurrence. They also highlight the uncertainties associated with the determination of masses for evolved stars.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics. 9 pages, 9 figures

papers.title: Normative and neural network models of multisensory integration
papers.summary: Animals continuously detect scents, sights and sounds, which their brains combine into diverse multisensory streams. Multisensory integration accelerates learning, increases reaction speeds and helps to resolve sensory ambiguities. In studying this process, the field has developed a continuum of models; from concise mathematical equations, with a handful of variables, to artificial neural networks, with billions of parameters. In this review, we divide this spectrum into two classes: normative models start from a hypothesis about how multisensory signals should be integrated, while neural network models aim to emulate how circuits could integrate them. Together, these models demonstrate that observers can integrate cues in a statistically optimal fashion, and help to explain experimental findings, including the diversity of multisensory neuron response profiles and network architectures. In this review, we provide a didactic overview of multisensory models, complete with accessible equations and Python code, and compare their assumptions and explanatory power. We detail what has been learned from these models. Finally, we discuss how the ideas and insights from classical theoretical models can be reconciled with those from artificial neural networks, and how this convergence should shape future research.

papers.title: EEG-World: Context-Conditioned Dynamics of the Watching Brain
papers.summary: Brain encoding models predict neural responses from audiovisual input, but typically overlook how ongoing brain activity shapes an individual's response. We introduce EEG-World, a recurrent world model that forecasts 10 seconds of EEG band-power dynamics from 6 seconds of preceding EEG and the subsequent audiovisual stimulus. Pretrained on continuous EEG, EEG-World learns shared neural dynamics and adapts to unseen individuals through lightweight subject-specific readouts. Using 2,584 hours of EEG from 78 participants, we show that nonlinear recurrent forecasting surpasses strong history-aware linear baselines at scale. EEG-World achieves a forecasting correlation of 0.261 versus 0.233 for the strongest history-and-video linear model, with a 3.3-second forecasting-horizon advantage. Its learned dynamics transfer to unseen participants, outperforming the linear baseline in 23 of 24 individuals after calibration. While ongoing EEG history accounts for most predictive performance, controlled stimulus analyses reveal an additional video-dependent component. This component also enables evaluation of visual representations, with V-JEPA 2 improving clip-locked prediction by 35% over combined CLIP and DINOv2 features. Our results demonstrate the value of transferable neural dynamics for individual EEG forecasting and highlight the importance of separating state-driven from stimulus-driven predictability.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables; appendix with 3 figures and 6 tables. Ancillary file lists the clip split

papers.title: Determining the electron-hole pair creation energy in a 4H-SiC p-n diode via X-ray spectroscopy
papers.summary: This paper reports on a measurement to determine the electron-hole pair creation energy in a 4H-SiC p-n diode. By measuring the spectra of several X-ray sources and comparing the response between the silicon-carbide diode and a commercial silicon diode, the electron-hole pair creation energy in 4H-SiC is determined to be (7.87 $\pm$ 0.09) eV. This is the first result obtained using X-ray spectra from several sources and including an estimate of the uncertainty. The result is in good agreement with studies of comparable devices.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in JINST, 9 pages, 4 figures

papers.title: Positive recurrence of weakly reversible stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics
papers.summary: We study finite stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics. A network is weakly reversible if every reaction lies on a directed cycle of complexes. We prove that, for arbitrary positive rate constants, the Markov chain of every such network is non-explosive and positive recurrent on each communicating class. This settles the long-standing chemical recurrence conjecture. The proof is by construction of a Lyapunov function. For a fixed choice of weights on the species, the function is the exponential of a weighted count of the molecules, adjusted by a bounded quantity which is defined through the paths of reactions leading back to a reference population, and which accounts for the species that are absent or scarce. Before the adjusted count can decrease, several preparatory steps may be needed. We count faster and slower steps separately, giving priority to paths that require fewer slow steps. Weak reversibility controls how competing reactions can change these counts. Finitely many choices of weights are then combined, and a minimization over a scale parameter gives a single function on each communicating class.

papers.title: Space Postman and ATLAS: Enabling Startup Participation in the Orbital Logistics Economy
papers.summary: Debris removal, in-orbit servicing and refuelling, last-mile delivery, in-space recycling and constellation deployment are separate businesses built on one planning problem: a single spacecraft must visit many targets whose orbital planes drift apart under Earth's oblateness, within a propellant tank and a deadline. Solving it well takes orbital dynamics and optimisation expertise that is rarely the core business of payload, tug or constellation companies; this keeps young operators out of orbital logistics or leaves them with costly hand-made schedules. This paper presents Space Postman, a planning service that turns a target list, a spacecraft and a time budget into a priced and, for rendezvous tours, verified mission plan, and ATLAS, a tug concept whose payload bay takes debris kits, client spacecraft or propellant. As most start-ups fail when the money runs out, the offer starts with software and adds the vehicle later. Two case studies show what it changes. For a notional follow-on to the DEXTER project, which develops ways to turn scrap aluminium into propellant, it plans a tour of ten high-risk upper stages that share one orbital shell: waiting alone cannot close the tour, an even split of the time costs a third more propellant, and time is the currency of the mission. For a tug that releases eight clients from one rideshare, the delivery order decides whether the tank suffices, and the plan prices each delivery by the plane it must reach. The planning engine reproduces the published winning solution of a public debris-removal benchmark at that solution's fidelity and, given the same launches, plans cheaper trajectories for most of them: an independent check for operators and investors. A calibrated planner paired with a payload-agnostic tug offers new operators a practical way into orbital logistics, provided its numbers are read at the fidelity at which they were obtained.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, 4 tables. Preprint of a paper accepted for presentation at the 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026), Antalya, Türkiye, 5-9 October 2026 (IAF paper IAC-26,E6,1,10,x115070)

papers.title: Atomic Policy: Composing Atomic Manipulation Skills with Agentic Reasoning
papers.summary: Long-horizon manipulation requires robots to translate task intent into physical interactions as the scene changes. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer semantic and spatial reasoning, while visuomotor policies provide fine-grained control. Yet ambiguous goals and dependencies between actions make their integration challenging. We introduce Atomic Policy, a framework that composes learned manipulation skills through grounded steering and execution feedback. A VLM estimates the symbolic state and goal, and a PDDL solver constructs a skill plan. An agentic harness steers each skill through language, visual pointing, or both, and verifies its outcome to guide phase transitions and replanning. A common phase-level interface supports specialized policies and generalist action models. Experiments in simulation and on a real robot show how Atomic Policy improves task following and supports recovery in complex, long-horizon manipulation. Project page: https://aaronzkd.github.io/atomic-policy/

papers.title: The Alma catalog of OB stars. IV. A massive star census of the Magellanic Clouds System
papers.summary: Context. The Magellanic Clouds System (MCS), comprising the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC) and the Magellanic Bridge (MB), offers a nearby laboratory for studying massive stars. Existing catalogs are limited by extinction, crowding, and incomplete cross-validation with the literature. Aims. We identify candidate stars with initial masses of roughly 8 solar masses or more, including O- and early-B-type stars, supergiants, luminous blue variables, and Wolf-Rayet stars. We aim to improve completeness in reddened and crowded regions and recover sources missed by large surveys. Methods. We combine Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry with SIMBAD, HST, and complementary optical and infrared surveys. We select candidates using color-magnitude and color-color diagrams, extinction tracks, Gaia astrometry and variability, and spectral classifications. We check for duplicates and multiple systems, include literature and HST-resolved sources without reliable Gaia counterparts, especially in 30 Dor, and derive synthetic Gaia photometry where Gaia measurements are incomplete. Results. ALS IV contains 51 954 massive star candidates: 36 506 in the LMC, 15 264 in the SMC, and 184 in the MB. It provides homogeneous identifiers and coordinates, multiwavelength photometry, astrometry, variability diagnostics, and spectral classifications where available. Complementary photometry and HST observations recover reddened and crowded sources missed by Gaia-based selections. The sample traces the main massive-star populations and prominent star-forming regions across the MCS. Conclusions. ALS IV provides the most comprehensive census of massive star candidates in the MCS and serves as a reference for massive-star studies and future surveys and Gaia releases.
papers.comment: The catalog is available for download via CDS

papers.title: From Grammar Deltas to Token Masks: Incremental Constrained Decoding under Runtime Grammar Evolution
papers.summary: Grammar-constrained decoding enables large language models to generate outputs that satisfy formal constraints, but in code and domain-specific language generation, the relevant constraints are not always fully available before decoding and may emerge progressively from new declarations, inferred type information, or runtime analysis feedback. Existing structured-decoding engines efficiently handle fixed, predeclared, or previously seen constraint structures; however, when a first-seen grammar update changes the parser state induced by an already committed prefix, the straightforward solution reconstructs the constraint state under the updated grammar, repeating parsing work already performed over the prefix. We introduce GramDelta, an incremental framework for constrained decoding with append-only runtime grammar updates. GramDelta maintains parse state over the committed prefix and propagates only changes induced by newly added grammar rules through historical dependencies, avoiding prefix replay. It then maps the updated parse state to exact next-token masks via compilation-free factorized projection over shared historical charts, avoiding per-update mask-cache recompilation. GramDelta therefore preserves the result of full reconstruction while making update cost sensitive to the actual impact of a grammar change. Experiments across four model configurations show that GramDelta adds negligible overhead without updates; under sustained runtime grammar evolution, it reduces median first-seen grammar-update latency by 10.7--11.5x and reduces the additional TPOT overhead over unconstrained decoding by 53.1--81.9% relative to the strongest reconstruction baseline. These results enable efficient constrained decoding when constraints progressively emerge and evolve with the generated prefix.

papers.title: Exploiting SU(2) Symmetry for Efficient Quantum State Preparation of Matrix Product States
papers.summary: Quantum computing offers a promising route to simulating strongly correlated systems, particularly for dynamical and spectral quantities whose classical computation can become prohibitively expensive. Fault-tolerant algorithms for these tasks, including real-time dynamics and phase estimation, assume efficient preparation of the initial many-body state, making state preparation an important bottleneck. Matrix product states obtained classically with the density matrix renormalization group can be compiled sequentially into fault-tolerant circuits. We exploit non-Abelian spin SU(2) symmetry in this compilation. By the Wigner-Eckart theorem, only the reduced tensors, which carry the variational information, need generic unitary synthesis. The magnetic structure is restored by Clebsch-Gordan transformations with analytically known angles. We benchmark the method on representative strongly correlated models, including the one-dimensional Hubbard model, quasi-one-dimensional Hubbard geometries, and Anderson impurity models, and perform fault-tolerant resource estimates using the Toffoli count as the primary cost metric. Across the systems considered, exploiting non-Abelian SU(2) symmetry reduces the Toffoli cost roughly threefold relative to U(1)-adapted compilation and by more than an order of magnitude relative to the standard dense compilation method. These results demonstrate how non-Abelian symmetries can substantially reduce the cost of transferring classically tractable many-body ground states to quantum computers, facilitating their use in quantum dynamics and energy estimation.

papers.title: Exact solution of the Bose-Fermi mixture along the unnesting line
papers.summary: A one-dimensional model of a Bose-Fermi mixture with contact repulsions is exactly solvable via nested Bethe ansatz. That formal solution is here simplified along a special line where the Bethe-ansatz equations can be unnested. The model solution is expressed in terms of the known solutions for the Lieb-Liniger model and the Yang-Gaudin model of attractive spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ fermions in the balanced case. We find explicit analytical results for the ground-state energy, the velocities of excitations, and the Drude weights at weak and strong interactions. At weak interactions, the special line corresponds to the parameter values where the isolated systems of free fermions and weakly interacting bosons have equal velocities.

papers.title: MRBench: Benchmarking Physical Necessity Reasoning in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Manipulation
papers.summary: Recent advances in multi-robot manipulation have shown how robots can collaborate to accomplish complex tasks. However, successful coordination does not reveal which robots are actually needed. The same task may require different teams as robot capabilities change, resources become unavailable, or objects replace robotic support. We argue that reliable multi-robot manipulation requires physical necessity reasoning: understanding what a task demands, which resources can fulfill those demands, and which are truly necessary. We introduce MRBench, a benchmark for physical necessity reasoning in heterogeneous multi-robot manipulation. It comprises eight tasks with distinct concurrency and reach constraints, each evaluated under five configurations that change the required resources while preserving the task goal. Our evaluation reveals that existing coordination agents perform well with reference teams but struggle when robot embodiments change or passive objects can replace robotic support. To address this gap, we propose MRScissors, which separates task requirements from measured physical capabilities and identifies minimal feasible teams through constrained search. Across two model backbones, MRScissors achieves 85.4% and 91.2% team-selection accuracy, outperforming the strongest baselines by 10.4 and 9.5 points, respectively. Together, these findings expose a critical gap between coordinating robots and understanding their physical necessity.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep
papers.summary: The ability to learn and generalize from limited experience, or sample efficiency, is a cornerstone of intelligence. How can we build language models that turn a few user interactions, a few snippets of unfamiliar code, or a handful of experimental results provided in context into knowledge that generalizes? Prior work has found that sleep, a process where the model performs $N$ recurrent forward passes to refine its representations of a chunk of context, can improve long-context reasoning (specifically, within SSM-attention hybrid models). We study whether this method also improves in-context adaptation on general, non-synthetic tasks for transformer language models. To this end, we pre-train language models up to 1.2B-parameters on up to 100B tokens with sleep mechanisms. Notably, longer sleep (i.e., using a larger number of recurrent forward passes $N$) enables the model to learn faster in-context on multiple few-shot algorithmic, question-answering tasks, while also achieving lower next-token prediction loss on out-of-distribution evaluations. On held-out code, models with $N=2$ and $N=4$ match the no-sleep baseline's loss using $2.10\times$ and $2.39\times$ fewer tokens in-context, respectively. More broadly, we view our work as a step toward building models that have better tradeoffs between in-context adaptation and decoding latency.

papers.title: Toward Solving the Galactic Foreground Problem in Gravitational-Wave Astronomy with Machine Learning
papers.summary: Space-borne gravitational-wave detectors will see tens of millions of Galactic binaries. Resolved, they would form a census of the Galaxy's ultracompact binaries unhindered by dust; unresolved, they are the dominant noise up to a few millihertz for massive black-hole binaries, extreme-mass-ratio inspirals and backgrounds from the early Universe. Separating the two requires the number of binaries, which is ill-defined because binaries exist at every amplitude. We make it an observable by defining a source as a binary above a signal-to-noise threshold. Neural flows count the binaries to within one in 99% of 1 microhertz intervals over 0.5-10 mHz, and nested sampling resolves them, even pairs closer than one frequency bin. The data themselves set a limit: a source is resolvable only if its signal pays for its own description, about 20 nats, which biases even ideal trans-dimensional samplers. Like the diffraction limit in imaging, this Bayesian confusion limit is set by the data rather than by the method, and it governs any superposition of weak sources, from radio surveys and pulsar timing arrays to super-resolution microscopy. For future space-borne detectors, the method turns the Galactic foreground into a definite, calibrated count of binaries with an analytic selection function, the basis for global fits and for tests of population models.

papers.title: Embodied Intelligence for Spectrum Map Construction in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
papers.summary: Accurate spectrum map construction by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is crucial for intelligent resource management in low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs). Although various construction approaches have been investigated, their performance often degrades under extremely sparse sampling because purely data-driven models may not capture the underlying propagation physics. To address these challenges, an embodied intelligence framework is proposed, which synergistically integrates closed-loop perception-cognition-execution (PCE) coupling and embodied exploration to achieve precise and efficient spectrum construction. Based on this framework, a corresponding embodied cognition and decision network (ECDNet) with three tightly coupled modules is designed. Specifically, by leveraging distance-aware convolutions, the semantic bridge, and adaptive feature alignment mechanisms, ECDNet establishes the bidirectional information flow between construction and decision-making. Simulation results show that ECDNet achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.787 dBm at 4.00% sampling under the non-revisiting spiral protocol. Furthermore, a practical UAV-based spectrum construction platform is developed and field-deployed to provide prototype-level evidence that the sensing, cognition, and action modules execute as a closed loop on size, weight, and power constrained UAV edge devices.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing

papers.title: Zone-folded Goldstone mode of the field-induced spin supersolid in the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet
papers.summary: The field-induced spin supersolid of the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet with single-ion and exchange anisotropy has so far been characterized only by static observables, among them a two-peak transverse structure factor. We compute its dynamic spin structure factors, and those of the neighboring phases, by stochastic analytic continuation of stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo data on a $16\times16$ lattice at inverse temperature $β=32$, at one field in each of the supersolid, the $m_z=1/2$ Ising plateau and the canted $XY$ phase. The supersolid has a single Goldstone mode, which the checkerboard folds onto both the ordering wave vector $\mathbf{Q}=(π,π)$ and $\mathbf{q}=(0,0)$, so that it appears in both spin channels at both points with one velocity $v=1.36\pm0.01$. The canted phase shows half of this pattern and the plateau none, the latter carrying instead a gapped magnon band and a two-magnon longitudinal continuum. Exactly at $\mathbf{Q}$ and $(0,0)$ the finite-lattice spectra are governed by a rotor tower of the condensate in the transverse channel and an Ising doublet of the checkerboard in the longitudinal one, both present at $\mathbf{Q}$ in the supersolid. Three parameter-free comparisons with the stiffness and the uniform susceptibility of the same runs, for the velocity, the sound-mode weight and the thermal decay of the rotor tower, tie the continued spectra to raw Monte Carlo observables. The folded Goldstone mode is the dynamical fingerprint of the supersolid.

papers.title: Supply Geometry, Learn Execution: Screw Attention for Zero-Shot Policy Transfer in Robot Manipulation
papers.summary: We present the Screw Attention Policy, a geometry-centric manipulation framework that supplies task geometry explicitly and learns only execution. The policy operates on object poses, relative SE(3) transforms, and joint screw axes provided by perception and robot models. The policy requires only 30K learned parameters. Trained entirely in simulation on a single robot arm, the policy generalises to new scene layouts, transfers zero-shot across robot embodiments, and deploys directly on a real robot, without adaptation or fine-tuning. It achieves 96% success on LIBERO, 85.8% under layout changes, 80.2% across five unseen robot arms, and 21 of 24 trials on a real robot. These results suggest that much of what manipulation policies learn at scale is geometric structure that can instead be supplied.

papers.title: Is Prosody Encoded in the Neural Audio Codec Mimi?
papers.summary: Neural audio codecs (NACs) have become a fundamental infrastructure for modern speech-language models, discretizing continuous speech signals into token sequences that enable large language models to process and generate audio. Most research evaluates codec quality at the decoding phase, assessing the naturalness of reconstructed speech. However, little research investigates what phonetic information is captured during encoding. In this paper, we investigated the potential correlates of prosody in the NAC Mimi, a codec used by conversational speech agents such as Moshi and Sesame and used in downstream tasks such as speech-to-speech translation (Hibiki).
papers.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, Published as a Speech Prosody 2026 conference paper, 569-573, doi: 10.21437/SpeechProsody.2026-115

papers.title: Accuracy of Noise Ceiling Estimators for Brain Scores
papers.summary: The internal activations of modern machine learning models align surprisingly well with the activities recorded in real brains. In the last five years, the alignment between encoding models and brain activities, often called brain scores, has steadily increased. Because brain recordings are noisy, there exists an upper bound to the brain scores that any model can achieve. This bound, called the noise ceiling, is crucial for two reasons: it determines whether further improvements in model performance are possible, and it enables meaningful comparisons of brain scores across benchmarks. The field has developed multiple approaches to estimate noise ceilings, but the statistical properties of existing estimators remain poorly understood, leaving it unclear in which experimental settings they provide reliable estimates. Here, we introduce a unified mathematical framework for brain recordings, use it to derive closed-form expressions for four commonly used noise ceiling estimators, and provide theoretical predictions for the behavior of each estimator. We validate the theoretical predictions with simulations that we compare to noise ceiling estimates in existing fMRI and EEG datasets. We find that the existing methods underestimate the true noise ceiling in different settings. We conclude with recommendations for best practice in different situations.
papers.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 35 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables

papers.title: Rough log-normal stochastic volatility with quadratic drift: second-moment stability and the martingale property under positive correlation
papers.summary: We extend the log-normal stochastic volatility model with quadratic drift to a fractional Volterra equation. The volatility has a unique global non-negative solution with finite moments on every finite horizon. With linear drift we derive the conditional first and second moments, expected integrated variance and conditional squared VIX. We give the exact threshold for a uniformly bounded second moment and the exponential growth rate above it. With positive quadratic damping the second moment is uniformly bounded for every admissible Hurst exponent and volatility of volatility. A separate bound on long-run expected integrated variance per unit time depends only on the drift parameters. Under the share measure the volatility beta offsets the quadratic damping. The price is a true martingale when damping covers beta. For a positive finite exponential mixture this condition is also necessary. The converse for a singular fractional kernel remains open. We illustrate calibration under positive correlation on observed Bitcoin and Ether option smiles and benchmark the simulation against exact moments. A marked order-flow construction relates multiplicative volatility noise to signed trade impacts arriving at a rate proportional to variance. A small state-dependent bias generates the quadratic drift. We establish a stopped diffusion limit for the constant kernel.

papers.title: Delta-Vega Hedging with Deep Reinforcement Learning: From Simulation to Reality
papers.summary: Hedging an option portfolio with the underlying asset alone leaves the position exposed to changes in volatility, which can be managed by trading another derivative, at higher transaction costs. We propose a deep reinforcement learning approach to hedge both price and volatility risk under discrete-time trading and transaction costs, by trading the underlying asset and a second, longer-dated option. We train the agent with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) on synthetic data from a stochastic volatility model, and restrict its state to quantities observable in the market, so that the policy learned in simulation applies directly to market data. In simulation, we validate the policy against semi-analytical Delta and Delta-Vega hedging benchmarks. PPO matches Delta-Vega's objective at baseline transaction costs and increasingly outperforms it as costs rise, with both two-instrument strategies consistently outperforming the single-instrument Delta hedge. On historical S&P 500 index option data, we benchmark our approach against practitioner Black-Scholes Delta and Delta-Vega hedging strategies. The two-instrument strategies roughly halve the profit-and-loss dispersion of the Delta hedge, and PPO attains a lower profit-and-loss volatility than Delta-Vega at comparable transaction costs. PPO holds more of the hedging option than Delta-Vega, in line with the stochastic-volatility model hedge, and its advantage is concentrated in high-volatility episodes.

papers.title: Packing the Bragg sphere: complete three-dimensional photonic band gaps at the refractive index of polymers (1.55)
papers.summary: Complete 3D photonic band gaps have so far been found only at refractive-index contrasts of about 1.9 and above, reached by rod-connected diamond lattice structures. Reciprocal-space design of quasiperiodic structures recently achieved considerable emission attenuation at much lower contrasts [L. Maiwald et al., Adv. Optical Mater. 10, 2100785 (2022)]. Here we implement systematic search and reciprocal-space design of periodic 3D structures with complete band gaps, solving a discrete optimization problem on an integer lattice. A gap above a high band needs the strongest Fourier components of the dielectric close to the Bragg sphere of that band. Crystals with large cells, started from Fourier peaks at the vertices of a polyhedron on this sphere and optimized against densely refined band edges, open complete gaps down to an index contrast of 1.55, that of common polymers against air. A rational approximant of an icosidodecahedron gave the most efficient location of the Fourier peaks among the polyhedra tested. Numerical calculations confirm the gaps over a resolution series, with band edges searched over the whole Brillouin zone. The best designs are connected porous networks, suited to a microwave test with printed polymer. A rigorous bound, valid for any structure, does not exclude gaps at lower index, and the next rational approximants of the icosidodecahedron, whose Bragg zones match bands 576 and 2440 almost exactly, point to where gaps at even lower contrast may be sought.

papers.title: Keypose or Dense? A Controlled Comparison of Action Representations for Stage-Structured Manipulation
papers.summary: Most imitation policies that predict chunks of future actions use the dense action representation, in which the chunk holds one control target per step. In stage-structured manipulation, where a task can be divided into stages with definable endpoints, the keypose action representation instead sets each step of the chunk to the endpoint of the stage that step belongs to, and a speed-capped servo supplies the motion. We compare the two in several simulated manipulation tasks and on a real robot, with the same chunk length and matched demonstrations, observations, policy architectures and update budgets; in simulation, each one's execution rule is selected on tuning scenes. When the simulated demonstrations are slowed, paused and rerouted, dense success falls sharply while keypose stays roughly level, across three policy architectures and with endpoints extracted from the recorded demonstrations; keypose also leads under object-size and position shift. With clean demonstrations, keypose leads only when they are scarce and is otherwise close to or behind dense across the simulated tasks, provided that the demonstrations and execution rule suit its executor; when they do not, it falls far below dense. The same dependence on the executor appeared on a real robot learning to open a drawer from human demonstrations: dense succeeded more often, and keypose improved substantially only after its executor's rotation and forward speed were adjusted to the demonstrations. These results suggest that keypose trades sensitivity to such variation in the demonstrations for sensitivity to execution that departs from them.

papers.title: Dynamical conditions for tilting Neptune during planetary migration
papers.summary: Giant planets are expected to form with near-zero obliquities, so that their current tilts must be the result of some post-formation processes. Capture into spin-orbit resonances has been shown to provide a viable mechanism for explaining the current obliquities of Jupiter, Saturn, and Uranus. We aim to determine whether specific configurations of a primordial satellite system of Neptune could have enabled the tilting of its spin axis during planetary migration. We modeled Neptune's secular spin-axis dynamics, including the presence of a primordial satellite system that enhanced the planet's precession constant. We numerically explored the conditions on the primordial satellite system that could trigger a spin-orbit resonance. We identified an open set in the parameter space that led to a successful tilting of Neptune. In particular, the total mass of the primordial system must have been $\geq 4\times 10^{-4}\,M_N$. A representative configuration consists of an inner satellite of mass $5\times 10 ^{-5}\,M_N$ and semi-major axis $35\,R_N$, and an outer satellite of mass $3.5\times 10 ^{-4}\,M_N$ and semi-major axis $100\,R_N$. Such a system could have survived during the unstable phase of the planetary migration if the gravitational encounters between Neptune and Uranus were not too close. The eventual ejection of the outer moon, possibly due to the encounter with a planetesimal, froze Neptune's obliquity to its current value. Neptune's current obliquity can be attained during planetary migration if the planet initially possessed a satellite system with a suitable architecture. The required satellite properties are not far from theoretical predictions and are consistent with recent scenarios proposed for the tilting of Uranus. Once the outer moon was ejected, the system matched a configuration suitable for the following capture of Triton and its fast evolution toward its current orbit.

papers.title: Simulator-as-Proxy World Model for Robot Manipulation
papers.summary: Video world models for robots are increasingly conditioned on a simulated or rendered proxy of the scene, on the assumption that the video will show what the proxy shows. Testing this assumption requires a proxy whose state is explicit and can be perturbed. We present SimPWM (Simulator-as-Proxy World Model): given a calibrated camera, it represents, from the first frame alone, the robot by its 3D model and the objects the gripper may touch as 3D points; a rule-based simulator with no trained parameters moves them under the actions, and a video model renders the result. SimPWM returns the realistic video together with the simulated state. We then freeze the simulated objects while the arm moves as recorded and check whether the video still shows the object lifted. On DROID episodes from unseen setups, the answer differs for the arm and for the objects. With each of three base video models, the arm follows the proxy (robot IoU 0.75-0.78, against at most 0.69 for end-to-end models); rendering the robot alone already gives this. What the simulated objects add is the object state: against a robot-only proxy, they cut missed pick-ups from 54% to 38%, and the video follows them only with some base models: on rigid objects, freezing them lowers the lift rate of MiniMax-H3, fine-tuned on episodes whose simulation agrees with the real video, from 42% to 10%, but that of LTX-2.3, trained on the same episodes, only from 57% to 49%, as if it inferred the grasp from the arm motion; more than half of the remaining lifts of MiniMax-H3 are of cloth and rope, which the simulator carries rigidly. With any base model, the simulated state records what the simulation did; under perturbed actions, a video that disagrees with it reveals that the video ignores the simulated state.
papers.comment: 27 pages. Project page: https://sim-pwm.pages.dev Code: https://github.com/TingtingLiao/SimPWM

papers.title: Recovery of Extended Modes from the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect Due to Local Nonlinearity on a Boundary
papers.summary: Localization in continuum spectra known as the non-Hermitian skin effect is widely believed to be a consequence of nontrivial topology of bulk bands. However, the robustness of the non-Hermitian skin effect against nonlinear effects is still a nontrivial problem. We here reveal that single-bond nonlinearity on a boundary can recover extended modes in a non-Hermitian tight-binding model. We propose and analyze a one-dimensional minimal model, where we introduce a nonlinear phase shift of a hopping term only at boundary sites. We also propose a possible photonic setup to dynamically observe the nonlinearity-induced extended modes as a steady state. Our results thus challenge the conventional notion of the non-Hermitian skin effect by revealing its dependence on nonlinear boundary conditions.

papers.title: Measuring Layer-wise Intrinsic Dimensionality of FFNs in LLMs via PCA
papers.summary: Modern large language models (LLMs) keep the feed-forward network (FFN) intermediate width identical across every layer, a convention inherited from the original Transformer. Yet mechanistic work suggests layers at different depths do qualitatively different work, raising a natural question: are their capacity demands also non-uniform, and if so, can a fixed parameter budget be allocated more wisely than uniformly? To probe this, we apply principal component analysis (PCA) to the input of each FFN down-projection and measure, for every layer, its intrinsic dimensionality as the smallest number of principal components needed to reconstruct the activation up to a fixed cosine similarity. Scanning 58 open-weight LLMs spanning 14 families and 70M to 72B parameters, we find a recurring middle-heavy profile in which middle layers carry higher intrinsic dimensionality than edge layers; the profile is robust to the calibration corpus, even across English and Chinese, and is largely preserved through post-training fine-tuning. As a direct test that this signal is structurally meaningful, we use it to guide width pruning in a knowledge-distilled student under a matched parameter budget: the PCA-guided allocation outperforms the uniform-width convention by +2.3 points on Qwen3-8B and +2.5 on Qwen2.5-3B, while lower-dispersion teachers show smaller gaps (+0.9 on Gemma-3-4B, +0.5 on LLaMA-3-8B), and a budget-matched inverted control does worst on all four teachers. Across these four teachers, the size of the gap tracks how unevenly the teacher's intrinsic dimensionality is distributed across layers (a single-number summary we call $σ_{99}$), and the advantage persists through downstream supervised fine-tuning. Code is available at https://github.com/naver-ai/lidf.
papers.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. 20 pages, 7 figures, 11 tables

papers.title: C3H: Compression-to-Consensus Criteria Hijacking in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems
papers.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are transforming recommender systems into content-aware decision systems. In these systems, multimodal compression and cross-modal fusion are often viewed as robustness-enhancing mechanisms against content manipulation, as compression can filter noisy signals and cross-modal consensus can suppress inconsistent anomalies. We challenge this assumption by showing that the same process can expose a compression-to-consensus (C2C) bias in ranking decisions. Signals that remain salient after compression and receive consistent support across modalities can gain disproportionate influence in candidate comparison, offering an exploitable direction for content manipulation. In this paper, we introduce C3H, a novel inference-time attack that exploits this vulnerability. Rather than relying on noisy perturbations or training-time poisoning, C3H promotes a target item by tailoring its multimodal content to align with the decision criteria implicitly expressed by the recommender. Extensive experiments demonstrate that C3H substantially increases target-item exposure while maintaining overall recommendation utility. Code is available at https://github.com/GuoweiGuan666/C3H.

papers.title: Beyond Fixed-Context Likelihood: Zero-Shot AI-Generated Text Detection via Context Perturbation Discrepancy
papers.summary: The same increase in token log probability from earlier context can be typical at one position and unusually large at another. We introduce Context Perturbation Discrepancy (CPD), a zero-shot detector that measures this gain relative to what a single pretrained language model expects. Keeping the passage fixed, CPD scores each observed token under its full prefix and under a short window of recent tokens. Under the full-prefix distribution, the expected gain equals the KL divergence from that distribution to the restricted-prefix distribution. CPD subtracts this expectation from each observed gain and scales the sum of the signed deviations by its analytical reference standard deviation. On unedited human and AI texts from GEN, DetectRL-X, and HART, subtracting the expected gain raises AUROC by 32.78-35.81 percentage points at the same variance scale. CPD outperforms seven zero-shot baselines, averaging 94.80% AUROC and 79.60% recall at a 5% false-positive rate. On original and edited HART passages, the same scores separate texts more clearly by draft origin than by the benchmark's final-expression labels (89.15% versus 65.50% AUROC). Code is available at https://github.com/BUPT-tyf/CPD.

papers.title: Space-Time Point Defects as Probes of Criticality: Application to the Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg Transition
papers.summary: At criticality, a local field acting at a single point in Euclidean space-time is irrelevant and induces a modulation in space and time that decays with twice its scaling dimension. This turns two-point correlation functions into one-point measurements: one operator insertion enters the Boltzmann weight, the other is measured. For the local magnetization the relation is exact at any source strength. Implemented in auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo, the approach yields the static spin susceptibility and imaginary-time-displaced correlations with unprecedented precision. We apply it to the Dirac-semimetal to antiferromagnetic-Mott-insulator transition of the half-filled $π$-flux Hubbard model. This lattice model provides a regularization of the $N_f=2$ Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg universality class. A finite-size scaling analysis estimates the critical exponents as $ ν=1.10(3)$ and $η_φ=1.09(4)$, close to field-theory predictions of $η_φ\simeq1$. Since $η_φ>1$, the equal-time structure factor at criticality does not diverge with the system size. Hence, the equal-time structure factor at the ordering wave vector is dominated by background contributions and cannot be used for extracting critical exponents. Consistently, the spin dynamics at the transition is strongly incoherent and the quantum Fisher information remains bounded.

papers.title: Contract2Reach: Discretization-Induced Contractive Dynamic Programming for High-Dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) enable undiscounted Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis for high-dimensional systems, but their performance can be sensitive to hyperparameter choices and the underlying system dynamics. We introduce Contract2Reach, which recasts undiscounted finite-horizon reachability as a sequence of contractive fixed-point problems solved by backward time marching. Our formulation combines discretized temporal and spatial derivatives to construct a contractive mapping without introducing a discount factor. Under standard assumptions, we prove that the exact scheme converges to the unique viscosity solution as both the temporal and spatial step sizes tend to zero. Unlike PINNs, our training fits rollout-based value targets via a single regression, without backpropagating through spatial value gradients. In the neural implementation, adaptive zero-level-set sampling and conservative target combination address high-dimensional sample sparsity and false positives, respectively. Experiments on a parameterized vertical drone, a 13D quadrotor, and a 40D publisher-subscriber system show competitive performance against PINNs-based baselines. Boundary evaluations on the vertical drone and publisher-subscriber systems demonstrate improved fidelity and reduced learning-rate sensitivity, revealing errors that volume-based metrics can miss.

papers.title: Large-Scale Streaming Portfolio Optimization with Pauli Correlation Encoding
papers.summary: Classical portfolio construction over large asset universes is a combinatorial selection problem that existing heuristics do not solve well at scale. Pauli Correlation Encoding (PCE) addresses this by representing the underlying clustering problem with far fewer qubits than one per asset, and a prior study showed it is competitive with classical methods on a single historical snapshot. This paper moves beyond that static test to a streaming deployment, in which the correlation structure and the portfolio are both re-estimated on a rolling basis, as a live rebalancing system would actually operate. We introduce two streaming variants -- PCE itself and a joint multi-cut variant, dPCE -- and evaluate both against a Buy & Hold baseline across window lengths, portfolio sizes up to several thousand assets, risk-aversion and transaction-cost settings, and measurement-shot budgets. Streaming PCE and dPCE consistently outperform the passive baseline, including during a market downturn where both lose money but PCE loses markedly less -- evidence that the method's value is not confined to rising markets. PCE also proves the more practical choice at scale, since dPCE's resource requirements and its sensitivity to rebalancing frequency both grow faster with portfolio size. We further report which operational choices -- rebalancing cadence, shot budget, and transaction-cost awareness -- matter most for a real deployment, and which matter less than commonly assumed.

papers.title: Risk-Informed Path Planning: Collision and Grounding Avoidance Application for Autonomous Surface Vessels
papers.summary: Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) must demonstrate safety before and during operations, necessitating online risk assessment to guide decision-making at sea. This paper presents a risk-informed Rapidly Exploring Random Tree Star (RRT*) path planner that integrates a Bayesian Belief Network (BBN) as an online risk model. The BBN evaluates the probability and severity distribution of hazardous events, which are aggregated into a bounded scalar risk index. During the search, this risk index is evaluated at sample points along candidate edges. The planner optimizes a composite cost function comprising path distance, heading change penalties, and accumulated risk, subject to a hard constraint enforcing a risk acceptance limit. Each search tree vertex stores the BBN posterior at its state, enabling the tree to function as an explainable risk map for individual hazards. We define design requirements for the BBN to serve as the risk model in this context and introduce a runtime model that translates replanning deadlines into strict limits on single risk calculation times. The planner is demonstrated in a simulated harbor entry scenario involving collision and grounding hazards. Measured run times validate that the planner operates within the computational bounds predicted by the runtime model for a single replanning cycle.

papers.title: Programmable multipartite entanglement analogues
papers.summary: Quantum entanglement underpins the quantum information science. Its multipartite forms distribute coherence across several subsystems, but controlling their composition and order is increasingly difficult as more subsystems participate. Classical nonseparable waves provide accessible analogues of these structures, although existing implementations largely fix the participating degrees of freedom through their generating architectures. Here we overcome this constraint by making multipartiteness itself programmable in electromagnetic fields. A spatiotemporal metasurface reconfigures the identity and number of coherently linked state spaces independently across polarization, frequency, orbital angular momentum, wavevector direction, and orthogonal envelope modes. We realize complete Bell-like and Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-like families from bipartite to five-partite order and exchange constituents at fixed order. To our knowledge, the five-partite state has the highest multipartite order experimentally realized in classical electromagnetic fields. These results establish the distribution of coherence across physical state spaces as a programmable property of classical waves and provide a platform for studying selected structures of multipartite quantum states without invoking quantum entanglement or nonlocality.

papers.title: Low-Power Spiking Neural Network Acceleration with Differential Time Representation: A Modular Hardware Framework
papers.summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer promising energy efficiency, making them well suited for energy-constrained applications. Much of their energy savings stems from the sparse encoding of spike trains. We show that spike trains can be represented more efficiently using Differential Time Representation (DTR), which requires fewer bits than Address-Event Representation (AER) or equidistantly sampled 1-bit spike trains. To support multiple input spike trains, we provide a rigorous proof that DTR sequences can be merged with low complexity. We also provide a set of modular hardware streaming components using this representation that can be flexibly connected to construct custom accelerator architectures for specific SNNs. Tailoring the hardware architecture to the selected SNN is streamlined by a Python framework combining the modular hardware components into a full SNN implementation. We use the framework to generate three accelerators for the Spiking Heidelberg Digits (SHD), Spiking Speech Commands (SSC), and PSMNIST benchmarks, each in a throughput-optimized parallel variant and a resource-reduced time-multiplexed variant. We report results for FPGA and ASIC implementations, the latter synthesized with a fully open-source flow targeting the predictive ASAP7 PDK. On the SHD dataset, the ASIC implementation reaches 92.46% classification accuracy, while sustaining $\approx{}$12,027 inferences per second at 20.37$μ$J per inference, exceeding the neuromorphic Loihi processor by 109$\times$ in throughput and 1.8$\times$ in energy efficiency. The corresponding FPGA implementation achieves $\approx{}$6,023 inferences per second without using DSP blocks. Across all three datasets, the synthesized ASICs reduce energy per inference by 27-37$\times$ relative to their FPGA counterparts, demonstrating that competitive SNN accelerators can be realized entirely within an open-source design flow.

papers.title: Classical sampling of verifiable graph-state quantum advantage experiments
papers.summary: Quantum computers are expected to outperform classical ones on some tasks, but a convincing demonstration must be both hard to reproduce classically and verifiable. A recent proposal achieves verifiability by preparing graph states with built-in error detection, so that the quality of the experiment can be certified without simulating it; hardness is added by measuring in a non-Clifford basis or by inserting T gates. We show that the two instances posted to demonstrate this proposal on IBM hardware can be sampled classically on eight graphics processing units, with higher quality than the hardware in comparable or shorter time. For the 70-qubit instance our samples are drawn from the ideal output distribution; for the 64-qubit instance with 314 T gates they come with a certified fidelity of at least 0.908, against 0.349 for the hardware. The reason lies in verification itself: T gates can only be placed where the error detection cannot see them, which pushes them towards the end of the circuit, where they add little classical cost. Our results identify the features that future verifiable advantage experiments must control.

papers.title: ReQOR: Operator-Discrepancy Subspace Repair for Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors in Large Language Models
papers.summary: Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors (QCBs) cause large language models (LLMs) to exhibit malicious behavior after quantization while remaining benign at high precision. Existing defenses often rely on security-guided configuration selection or iterative optimization, but do not identify which quantization-induced changes should be repaired. We isolate module-local quantization effects from upstream drift by evaluating the high-precision and quantized versions of each module on identical states from the quantized inference trajectory, and formulate QCB defense as repairing the resulting same-state operator discrepancies. We propose ReQOR, a training-free defense that identifies the dominant directions of these discrepancies on benign calibration data and restores the full-precision computation along them in closed form, yielding a factorized residual adapter. ReQOR uses neither attack information nor gradient-based optimization and supports both full-span and low-rank repair. Experiments across four LLMs, three PGD-based QCB attacks, three malicious behaviors, and three quantization formats show substantial QCB mitigation while largely preserving benign utility. In additional experiments on a non-PGD outlier-injection attack, existing baselines largely fail, whereas ReQOR remains effective. Further analysis shows that dominant operator-discrepancy directions provide more effective and rank-efficient repair than rank-matched random, low-energy, or raw weight-error directions, while low-rank ReQOR reduces deployment memory overhead.

papers.title: Heat Reduction in Erbium-Doped Microresonator
papers.summary: We investigate anti-Stokes fluorescence in a 106-micrometer-diameter silica whispering-gallery-mode microresonator coated with erbium-doped sol-gel, assessing its potential for reduced optical heating. Near-infrared fluorescence spectra acquired under pulsed excitation near 1.55 micrometers exhibit a mean emitted photon energy above the pump photon energy. Measurements over a temperature range of 25 to 62 degrees Celsius show that the mean fluorescence photon energy increases with externally controlled temperature. The measured pump-wavelength dependence is consistent with an absorption-weighted spectral model, which predicts an optimum near 1562.65 nm for the investigated spectral figure of merit. Resonance-dependent emission patterns further motivate a dual-frequency pumping scheme using two higher-order whispering-gallery modes. Calculated time-averaged field profiles indicate that complementary modal distributions can provide more uniform excitation near the equator. These results characterize spectral conditions relevant to fluorescence-based heat reduction and suggest a route toward improved spatial pump coverage. Demonstrating net optical refrigeration requires additional measurements of absorbed pump power and an independent thermal readout.

papers.title: Multiscale Zoom-in Lattice Simulation for Inflation
papers.summary: Lattice simulations are a powerful tool for studying the nonlinear evolution of inflationary fluctuations. The exponential expansion, however, makes it challenging to cover a broad range of scales relevant for the dynamics, limiting how many e-folds a single fixed grid can follow. We develop a three-dimensional zoom-in lattice method to follow inflationary fluctuations over a broad range of scales from the adiabatic subhorizon regime through horizon crossing. Every few e-folds, the grid is refined into one or more subgrids, with small-scale power injected and large-scale fluctuations inherited from previous generations. Each zoom shifts the resolved band while keeping its dynamic range fixed. This extends the duration over which lattice simulations can follow inflationary fluctuations from a few e-folds to tens of e-folds. In a Starobinsky benchmark evolved for 50 e-folds, the curvature power spectrum agrees with linear theory. In a model with an oscillatory feature, the zoom-in simulations recover the peak seen in a high-resolution fixed-grid run and show scale-dependent non-Gaussianity.

papers.title: Convex computation of cost bounds for data-driven nonlinear optimal control
papers.summary: The paper addresses the optimal control problem of an input-affine polynomial system with an unknown (state-dependent) input matrix affecting the control effectiveness. Under assumptions on the existence of a data set and the Lipschitz continuity of the unknown part {of the dynamics}, an uncertainty set is constructed and used to adapt the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation towards a data-driven formulation. We solve it for the best-case scenario, thus giving a lower bound on the best cost achievable by means of a feedback control policy. After relaxing it into a moment-SoS hierarchy of semidefinite programs, a control law is extracted from the primal on moments and compared with other benchmark methods in a numerical application.

papers.title: Baker-Akhiezer functions for Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system
papers.summary: The Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system is a counterpart of the trigonometric Ruijsenaars integrable system (associated with the root system $A_n$) for the root system $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$. It depends on the standard Macdonald parameters $q$ and $t$ as well as the Koornwinder (Askey-Wilson) parameters $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$. Different specializations of the parameters connect it to the other classical root systems from the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family. The eigenfunctions of the Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system are the symmetric Koornwinder polynomials; for certain values of the parameters $t$, $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ they coincide with the sum over the Weyl group of the Baker-Akhiezer functions introduced by O.A.\,Chalykh for the classical root system $BC_n$. The main idea behind this paper is to elucidate Chalykh's formalism and apply it to other affine root systems. We define Baker-Akhiezer functions for all root systems in the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family. We also present some explicit expressions for Baker-Akhiezer functions.

papers.title: Lattice models of chiral random motion: A short review
papers.summary: Chirality, a systematic rotational bias, is ubiquitous in many random motion patterns, from bacteria cells, that swim in circles near surfaces and spinning colloids, to charged particles diffusing under the influence of magnetic fields. In two dimensions, chirality renders random transport \textit{odd}: the diffusion tensor acquires an antisymmetric part that leaves the mean-squared displacement invariant but modifies fluxes and boundary currents. Lattice models for random motion are a natural setting to study chirality, since they are exactly solvable, connect directly to heterogeneous media, cellular automata, and programmable robots, and in discrete time admit fully chiral limits with a localised bulk and edge transport. Lattice walks with a rotational bias have been introduced in different communities several times since 1960, yet without a common language or conceptual connection between them. Here we review these models from the perspective that on the lattice, chirality requires memory. Taking the recently introduced chiral random walk model as a template, we describe the walker with an internal degree of freedom. With a chiral biased updating rule, the full diffusion tensor of this chiral walker turns odd. Within this picture, we can unite persistent and chiral walks, run-and-tumble motion, and cyclic random motions in one framework. We discuss how the memory is followed into the environment; in Lorentz lattice gases, kinetic and rotor walks, and random odd environments; and into the path; in spiral self-avoiding walks.

papers.title: What it is to Obey
papers.summary: Prior to agents taking part in a simultaneous-move game, a designer commits a device that sends signals to each of the agents, evaluating the resulting set of equilibria according to a (Hausdorff-)continuous function. In games of incomplete information I show that it must be without loss of optimality for the designer to restrict attention to direct obedient devices if and only if she assumes her preferred equilibrium will be played. In games of complete information, I characterize the monotone evaluations, which include both the maximally optimistic one and the maximally pessimistic one.

papers.title: Quantum Community Detection for Data Analysis
papers.summary: Community detection offers an alternative to conventional methods for data analysis tasks such as feature selection and clustering, and detecting communities with quantum algorithms is a promising avenue for quantum speedup. We investigate quantum spectral community detectors, such as the modularity-matrix algorithm deteQt, in pipelines for both tasks. We first generalise deteQt to multiple communities by recursive bisection, and show that it recovers planted communities, and hence redundant features, in synthetic and small datasets. We then propose projeQt, which applies a spectral filter to the encoded modularity matrix through the quantum singular value transformation, retaining higher-order eigenvectors that deteQt does not use. projeQt acts on the generalised modularity matrix and extracts several communities at once, without recursion, by k-means clustering of a Gram matrix built from quantum state overlaps. On MNIST we demonstrate both pipelines, selecting informative pixels and classifying images directly by clustering, and find them competitive with standard community detectors.

papers.title: Impact of Taylor-Aris dispersion on chemical patterns in confined channel flows
papers.summary: Chemical patterns form through non-linear interactions between different species. We study how confined channel flows affect pattern formation using the Brusselator as a paradigmatic activator-inhibitor model. An invariant-manifold method for slender channels reduces the advection-diffusion-reaction equation to one spatial dimension, with species transported at the mean flow velocity and molecular diffusivities replaced by the classical Taylor-Aris dispersion coefficients. We obtain the phase diagram as a function of the Péclet number (i.e., the relative strength of advection to diffusion), the channel slenderness, and the diffusivity ratio of the species. Our analytical results demonstrate that the classical Turing criterion can become inverted at large Péclet numbers and, thus, channel flow can trigger pattern formation even when the molecular diffusivities violate the classical Turing condition, and conversely destroy pre-existing patterns. Both predictions are confirmed by direct numerical simulations, which show advected stripe patterns, whose wavelength can be predicted by our reduced theory, as well as oscillatory dynamics. These findings highlight that hydrodynamic flows can modify chemical mixing and thereby profoundly affect pattern formation in channel geometries.

papers.title: ASCENT: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Advancing Stepwise Diagnostic Reasoning in Large Language Models on Common Clinical Scenarios
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) excel at medical question answering yet are rarely evaluated on the stepwise diagnostic reasoning that defines real clinical workflows, where impressions are revised as information accumulates. We build Annotated Stepwise Clinical rEasoning for NaturalisTic Diagnosis (ASCENT), a clinician-annotated benchmark and training resource of 3,078 stepwise problems derived from MedQA-USMLE that decomposes each vignette into EMR-aligned steps (Findings, Impression, supporting Rationale), enabling evaluation of intermediate reasoning under incomplete information. Experiments and training with ASCENT revealed insights into how current LLMs handle stepwise diagnostic reasoning. Even strong reasoning models that perform well on MedQA-USMLE leave substantial headroom on ASCENT, and general-purpose frontier models trail further, exposing a persistent gap between fully informed and stepwise diagnosis. Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-7B and 32B on ASCENT yields measurable F1 gains over both pre-trained and HuatuoGPT-o1 CoT-trained baselines, with gains driven primarily by precision. Complementary robustness analyses (counterfactual perturbation, format-vs-content control, judge agreement, and rollout) further show that ASCENT-fine-tuned models rely on the diagnostic content of prior impressions rather than imitating their output format, while error propagation under rollout remains a key challenge for clinical deployment.
papers.comment: Published in Proceedings of the 7th Conference on Health, Inference, and Learning (CHIL 2026), PMLR 333:404-426. 23 pages, 8 figures, 12 tables. Data and code: https://github.com/naver-ai/ascent
papers.journal: Proceedings of the 7th Conference on Health, Inference, and Learning, PMLR 333:404-426, 2026

papers.title: A Gauge Pathway to an Ultralight Axion through a Hidden Portal
papers.summary: We study a gauge realization of an ultralight axion with a hidden $SU(2)$ interaction, an Abelian vector portal, a charged Higgs and a Stückelberg field. The vector absorbs one scalar combination and leaves a physical phase. Its normalization is fixed by the Higgs and Stückelberg scales, while hidden confinement generates its mass. Keeping this phase ultralight requires an additional symmetry: the displayed gauge charges alone allow large phase-dependent scalar interactions. We quantify the suppression required of these interactions. Pure-$SU(2)$ lattice results relate the susceptibility to physical confinement scales; one- and two-loop running illustrate the dependence on the chosen high-energy coupling. We derive the coherent radiation-era density and exhibit an initial angle giving the reference dark-matter abundance for $F_χ\simeq10^{17}\,\GeV$ and zero-temperature mass $m_{χ,0}=3\times10^{-20}\,\eV$. We follow the confined population through number-changing and number-conserving limits and bound its energy contribution. An illustrative inflaton background satisfies the stated vacuum and isocurvature tests, conditional on control of a large portal correction to its potential. Its cold hidden history requires a hidden-to-visible reheating fraction near $5\times10^{-12}$, whose microscopic origin remains an input. A second, gauge-anomaly-free model gives the same physical phase scale using two charged Higgs singlets. These constructions specify conditional cosmological examples and the additional protection and reheating mechanisms needed to complete them.

papers.title: Support2Sim: Visually Faithful Real2Sim with Stable Object Supports
papers.summary: Reconstructing a scene for physics simulation requires recovering its spatial layout and the support relationships that govern its behavior. We present Support2Sim, a Real2Sim system that reconstructs simulation-ready scenes from a single RGB image. Our design objective is to maximize source fidelity, support realization, and stability within a practical time budget for scene generation. Support2Sim infers a support graph, which a contact-guided pose initializer uses to propose poses for objects with multiple supports. The initializer generates and ranks candidates by geometric fit and source-image agreement. A coarse-to-fine refiner allocates a fixed search budget across supported objects and evaluates pose updates with physics rollouts. After an accepted update, it searches from the new pose at a finer translation and rotation scale. We benchmark our method on 50 scenes spanning four datasets. Compared with the strongest baseline, Support2Sim improves source-mask IoU after 10 seconds by 21.4 pp, realizes 87.1% versus 73.2% of intended supports, and reduces mean object drift from 79.6 to 45.3 mm. See our project page at https://support2sim.github.io for more details.

papers.title: Robust inverse dielectric design of skin phantoms for implantable wireless link evaluation
papers.summary: Skin phantoms support reproducible evaluation of implantable wireless links, yet published complex permittivities of skin predict different propagation losses. We formulate a robust inverse design to determine a homogeneous phantom permittivity that minimizes the largest channel-loss difference across selected skin reference models, incidence angles and both transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic polarizations. Computed candidates and analytical lower bounds bracket the optimal mismatch and constrain the critical depth. Across seven frequencies from 5 to 500 GHz, the minimax mismatch at 1.3 mm ranges from 1.13 to 13.72 dB. For a 3 dB tolerance, suitable permittivities exist at every investigated depth at 5 GHz, while critical depths at the other frequencies range from 0.23 to 1.01 mm. Only one of seven material cases from the literature meets a 6 dB tolerance at 1.3 mm. These results translate channel-loss tolerances into quantitative design criteria for skin phantoms used in implantable wireless link evaluation.

papers.title: Conformality lost in Anderson localization in infinite dimensions, and regained in finite dimensions: a phenomenological theory of the Anderson transition in high dimensions
papers.summary: We show that the recent works on Anderson localization when the number of spatial dimensions $d\to\infty$ can be framed into the scenario dubbed it conformality lost [Kaplan et al., Phys. Rev. D 80, 125005 (2009)], which occurs when two fixed points of the RG collide and become complex. This framing makes it natural for a two-parameter scaling flow à la Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) to control all the observables of the theory as conjectured in [Vanoni et al., PNAS 121, e2401955121 (2024)]. We also use this as a starting point for an $ε$ expansion of the RG equations in $ε=1/d\ll 1$, and find phenomenological RG equations which fit the numerical results in dimensions $d\gtrsim 4$.

papers.title: Mixing and Preserving Properties of Non-van der Waals 2D Materials in Sandwich-like Heterostructures
papers.summary: Heterostructure interfaces created by stacking two-dimensional (2D) materials outline an appealing route towards achieving advanced electronic and magnetic functionalities at the nanoscale. Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) sandwich-like heterostructures (HSs) are build out of non-vdW 2D materials derived from non-layered crystals and establish a new frontier enabling strong interfacial coupling.
