Employing ab initio density functional theory (DFT), we investigate two classes of such trilayer HSs: purely non-vdW assemblies and hybrid vdW/non-vdW/vdW stacks. We show that non-vdW sandwiches undergo pronounced geometric reconstruction forming chemically bonded interfaces with large absolute binding energies up to an order of magnitude larger than those of conventional vdW HSs. These strong interactions drive extensive electronic hybridization, band gap renormalization, and tunable interlayer magnetic coupling. In contrast, vdW encapsulation largely protects the intrinsic atomic and electronic structure of the non-vdW sheet from the environment , while enabling charge transfer doping of the vdW layers. Our results thus establish sandwich HSs a versatile interface design platform, spanning interaction regimes from weakly perturbed encapsulation to strongly interacting chemically bonded systems with emergent electronic and magnetic behavior.

papers.title: AG-WAM: Attention-Guided World Action Model for Accurate and Efficient Robot Manipulation
papers.summary: Recently developed World Action Models (WAMs) jointly predict future observations and robot actions, providing predictive context for control. However, existing WAMs typically learn implicit attention allocation with limited explicit action-relevant attention guidance, leading to limited performance. To unleash strong capabilities of WAMs, we introduce explicit attention guidance as a unifying principle and propose our Attention-Guided WAM (AG-WAM), an end-to-end framework with three plug-and-play attention guidance modules that directly reformulate internal attention paradigm in WAMs: the Content-Adaptive Predictive Attention module, the Guidance-Point Visual Attention module, and the State-Conditioned Text Attention module. Without any external plugin module adopted, our end-to-end framework with the unifying principle of explicit attention guidance boosts the accuracy and efficiency of WAMs. Without using any private embodied training data, our AG-WAM establishes new state-of-the-art performance on multiple public robotic manipulation benchmarks including LIBERO-X, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin-2.0, significantly outperforming other methods, even those using massive private embodied training data by a notable margin, meanwhile notably improving training and inference efficiency.

papers.title: Parton Branching evolution in updfevolv: NNLO spacelike evolution in the ZM-VFNS and NLO timelike evolution with heavy-flavour matching
papers.summary: We describe two extensions of the Parton Branching (PB) method as implemented in updfevolv: the next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) spacelike DGLAP evolution of parton densities in the zero-mass variable-flavour-number scheme (ZM-VFNS), and the leading and next-to-leading order (LO, NLO) timelike evolution of fragmentation functions, including the heavy-flavour matching conditions at the quark thresholds. We summarise the timelike PB formalism - momentum sum rule, Sudakov form factor, branching chain and kinematics. We give implementation details needed for the PB formalism to reproduce the semi-analytical solutions of APFEL for all flavours, including heavy quarks at threshold. This note supplements the updfevolv manual and is a technical release note for updfevolv version 2.6.0.

papers.title: Seeing to Drive on a Single Board: Attention-Free Depth for Onboard Robot Navigation
papers.summary: A small ground robot can carry one camera and a few watts of compute, but the depth foundation models that could turn that camera into a range sensor are vision transformers sized for GPUs. We bring one to a Raspberry Pi 5 with the Hailo-8L, an accelerator that runs every layer in integer arithmetic, attention included. Quantised for it, Depth Anything V2 loses large parts of the scene, and we measure why: at 449 tokens, 91% of softmax weights fall below one int8 step while carrying 17-33% of the attention mass. Our answer is to distil, not quantise. An attention-free ResNet-34 U-Net student of Depth Anything V2-Large (24.5M parameters) runs at 27.1 FPS on the chip, its int8 output matches its float twin (Pearson 0.99993), and on held-out scenes of its simulated yard it is the most accurate depth network on the chip (AbsRel 0.269 against 0.354-0.530). On 1,000 stereo-verified points of a real outdoor drive it is not resolvably different from the vendor's Depth Anything V2-Small build, while running faster (27.1 vs 21.6 FPS). Ranging obstacles by where they meet the floor needs only the camera height, so mapping, hybrid-A* planning and SLAM run on the Pi's own CPU. In real-time hardware-in-the-loop tests in a Gaussian-splat reconstruction of a real yard, the stack reaches the goal without contact in 7.9$\pm$1.1 of 10 scenes, against 9.2$\pm$0.4 with exact obstacles, and in 7.7$\pm$0.7 on its own pose with simulated wheel odometry (ten seeds each; 8.2$\pm$0.4 with the real Pi and Hailo-8L in the loop, five seeds). The source code, pre-trained models and data are available at https://github.com/itaim18/DANIEL.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 14 figures, 5 tables. Code, models and data: https://github.com/itaim18/DANIEL

papers.title: Semidefinite Programming for Cold-Start GNSS Doppler-Based Alignment: A Comparison with Nonlinear Least Squares
papers.summary: Initial attitude alignment between local navigation frames and the Earth-centered Earth-fixed (ECEF) frame is a critical prerequisite for multi-sensor integrated navigation, such as Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)/inertial/odometry fusion, before global and local measurements can be jointly processed. While GNSS Doppler-based alignment eliminates the need for carrier-phase ambiguity resolution or multi-antenna hardware, solving this non-convex problem via local nonlinear least squares (NLS) suffers from local minima, whereas direct semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxation incurs high latency and omits local covariance outputs. This study systematically compares NLS and SDP on a unified maximum-likelihood Doppler objective across Monte Carlo simulations and three real-world driving datasets. We demonstrate that attaching a modular dual SDP certifier to a standard manifold NLS solver recovers the global accuracy of direct SDP within 0.001 degrees, reduces real-world 95th-percentile yaw errors from over 86 degrees down to 2.88 degrees to 4.70 degrees, and cuts median solve times by up to an order of magnitude while preserving native Jacobian covariances. We conclude that candidate-driven certification bridges local estimation and global optimization due to two structural advantages: (1) our theoretical comparison reveals that SDP relaxation enlarges the feasible region while preserving the lifted cost, allowing Lagrangian duality to verify whether a fixed NLS candidate attains the global lower bound without invoking a full SDP solver, and (2) the candidate-driven architecture acts as a non-intrusive module that plugs directly into existing navigation pipelines without replacing the local estimator, preserving native tangent-space covariance outputs and low typical latency.

papers.title: The impact of phase transitions on dilepton production
papers.summary: We calculate dielectron yields at beam energies relevant for the CBM experiment at FAIR and the STAR Beam Energy Scan. The production of intermediate mass dielectrons is expected to increase in presence of a phase transition due to the latent heat. In this work, we use the SMASH+vHLLE hybrid model to quantify this enhancement in two scenarios: with a toy equation of state consisting of the Bag Model and Hadron Resonance Gas, separated by a Maxwell-constructed transition; and with a more realistic equation of state containing a critical endpoint, based on the 3D Ising universality class. We confirm that the dilepton yield increases when the system passes through a first-order phase transition, by about 7% in the realistic scenario.

papers.title: Red-Teaming a Sovereign LLM, Its Reasoning and Its Training Stages
papers.summary: Open-weight large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed for applications with sensitive information. We investigate whether confidentiality instructions in system prompt can protect such information. We red-team Apertus v1.5, an open sovereign LLM, and five other model families across six languages and reasoning modes. We use synthetic personal records to evaluate direct disclosure, correction baits, yes/no verification, derived-value queries, reasoning leakage and authorisation checks. We also explore copyright attribution, historical misrepresentation and stereotyping. Despite confidentiality instructions, Apertus 8B and 70B leak information in 96% and 95% of requests, respectively, in correction-bait attacks. Verification and derived-value queries also expose protected information without necessarily revealing identifiers. Moreover, reasoning traces can leak confidential records even when final answers withhold them. Our experiments also show that post-training does not consistently improve safety. Our findings demonstrate that system prompts alone cannot ensure confidentiality and highlight the need for multilingual reasoning-aware safety evaluations.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Topological High-Harmonic Spectroscopy for Characterizing Crystal Symmetries and Nonlinear Responses
papers.summary: Structured light has emerged as a unique tool for probing nonlinear light-matter interactions. Particularly interesting is its interaction with anisotropic media, such as crystalline materials, whose anisotropic responses encode information about their electronic properties. Recently, topological high-harmonic spectroscopy was introduced as an all-optical approach to extract the anisotropic nonlinear response of graphene from harmonic spatial intensity profiles. Here, topological high-harmonic spectroscopy is combined with artificial intelligence (AI) to retrieve the anisotropic non-linear response and crystal symmetry of atomically thin materials. A convolutional neural network is trained and validated to learn the inverse mapping between harmonic far-field intensity profiles and the nonlinear response of materials exhibiting different rotational symmetries. Comparisons with microscopic high-harmonic-generation simulations demonstrate the accurate retrieval of distinct effective nonlinear responses in single-symmetry crystals, such as single-layer graphene and bilayer graphene with different stacking orders, and in crystals exhibiting multiple symmetry components, such as monolayer hexagonal boron nitride. Macroscopic high-harmonic-generation simulations assess the robustness and applicability limits of the technique. These results establish AI-assisted topological high-harmonic spectroscopy as a fast, contactless tool for characterizing nonlinear optical responses and crystal symmetries without phase-resolved measurements, opening prospects for applications to complex systems such as polycrystals and van der Waals heterostructures.

papers.title: Effect of humidity and phase transition on turbulent diffusion of droplets and water vapour in atmospheric turbulent flows
papers.summary: We investigate the effect of humidity on turbulent diffusion of droplets and water vapour in atmospheric turbulent flows taking into account the effect of phase transitions on turbulent transport. We find that the coefficients of turbulent diffusion of droplets and water vapour decrease with increase the turbulent Damköhler number (the ratio of turbulent time in the integral scale and phase transition time for condensation of water vapour), while the coefficients of the mutual turbulent diffusion that describe the turbulent cross effects increase with this parameter. For large turbulent Damköhler number, the coefficient of turbulent diffusion of droplets is strongly depleted when the evaporation of droplets is much faster than the condensation of water vapour. The obtained theoretical relationships are potentially useful in modelling applications in the atmospheric turbulence.

papers.title: Nonreciprocal state-selective splitting of eigenstates at a polarization exceptional point
papers.summary: Non-Hermitian photonic systems can be engineered to exhibit exceptional points (EPs), where eigenvalues and eigenstates coalesce. Although perturbations near EPs have mainly been characterized through eigenvalue splitting, the branch-resolved evolution of the coalesced eigenstates under a tunable reciprocity-breaking perturbation remains less systematically explored. Here, we show that tunable nonreciprocal coupling can produce state-selective splitting of the coalesced eigenstates near a second-order polarization EP. Using temporal coupled-mode theory, we find that the corresponding off-diagonal perturbation produces a triangular Hamiltonian in the circular-polarization basis. In the ideal limit, one eigenstate remains pinned to the EP state, whereas the other is continuously reoriented by the perturbation. In a realistic scattering system, residual reverse-polarization conversion weakly displaces the nominally pinned branch, resulting in quasi-pinning. We numerically demonstrate this mechanism in a reflective magneto-optical metasurface supporting a circular-polarization EP of the reflection matrix near 582 nm. Full-wave simulations show that a perpendicular magneto-optical bias leaves one reflection eigenstate close to the EP state while reversibly displacing the other on the Poincare sphere. This asymmetric eigenstate evolution manifests as a magnetically tunable circular-dichroic reflection response. Our results establish a nonreciprocal route to state-selective eigenstate control near polarization EPs.

papers.title: TWIN-1: A new 185 to 350 MHz Two-Element Radio Interferometer for Solar Observation at Gauribidanur
papers.summary: We present details of a new two-element radio interferometer, namely the TWIN, developed for routine monitoring of solar events at the Gauribidanur Observatory (77.428°E, 13.603°N) between 185 MHz and 350 MHz. This interferometer is built using custom-built antennas, an indigenous RF front-end consisting of LNAs, power combiners, and high-gain amplifiers, and RF over fiber signal transport modules. A data capture system was developed using a commercial digital storage oscilloscope and controlled with custom-designed Python-based tools. The oscilloscope digitises the RF signals with a time resolution of 0.8 ns, bursts of 9952 time samples, with a nominal duty cycle of 3 seconds, and the resultant data is collected on a remote computer. Specialised tools were developed to analyse the data and detect solar events. The interferometer has been operational since July 2023. In our analysis, we have detected several solar events from the ongoing Solar Cycle 25. This paper outlines the design philosophy, signal flow, commissioning and validation, results from a solar event, and future plans for data capture, data analysis, and archival.

papers.title: The W Transform: an additional powerful tool for astrophysical time-series analysis
papers.summary: This work introduces the W Transform (WT) for astrophysical applications and explores its similarities and differences to the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), in photometric stellar light curves (LCs). We tested both techniques on synthetic data, producing LCs with different noise levels and numbers of gaps, and applied them to LCs from TESS space mission. The analysis focused on six stars: the solar analog TIC 276293046, the ultra-cool dwarf TIC 359892714, the $γ$ Dor pulsator TIC 164173105, the eclipsing binary TIC 355151781, the hosting planet star TIC 142276270, and the brown dwarf TIC 102076870. Overall, the results were in agreement, except for stars with LCs presenting sector-to-sector differences in structures or changes in the number of gaps, reflecting time-dynamic effects in the same target, which affect how time-dependent variability features appear in the time-frequency representation. For such LCs, the WT spectra are more stable and accurate in recovering signal amplitudes than the CWT maps, which exhibit distortions and limitations, showing that the inherent flexibility of the WT method in adjusting the dominant frequency could enhance time resolution even in LCs with complex or variable structures. We conclude that the WT is a robust tool for the analysis of stellar LCs, and that both methods may complement each other in an in-depth analysis of a periodic astrophysical signal. The present results suggest that the WT is a robust and accurate tool for analyzing stellar LCs, expanding the range of numerical techniques available for analyzing different stellar periodic phenomena from photometric observations.
papers.comment: 25 pages, 11 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ

papers.title: A Hybrid Analytical-Neural Residual Surrogate for Fast Radio Propagation Prediction over Irregular Terrain
papers.summary: Fast prediction of radio-wave propagation over irregular terrain is important for coverage analysis in mountainous environments, where many terrain and antenna configurations must be evaluated repeatedly. High-fidelity split-step parabolic equation (SSPE) solvers can capture terrain-induced shadowing and interference, but their computational cost is high for repeated planning studies. Learning-based surrogates reduce this cost, but direct field regression asks the network to learn both analytically tractable propagation trends and terrain-dependent residual structure. This paper proposes a hybrid analytical-neural residual surrogate that separates these two parts. A deterministic analytical baseline represents free-space spreading, antenna directivity, modified knife-edge diffraction, and terrain-aware specular reflection, while a compact coarse-to-fine neural network predicts the residual field. The network uses baseline-derived guidance channels, anisotropic convolutions, and feature-wise antenna conditioning to match the directional structure of terrain propagation fields. On synthetic SSPE data at 1.0 GHz, the proposed model achieves an MAE of 2.1061 dB, compared with 3.3955 dB for a standard U-Net and 3.2560 dB for a reproduced physics-guided CNN, while reducing the average inference time to 11.30 ms per sample. A zero-shot test at 1.8 GHz gives an MAE of 2.8692 dB without retraining, and a case study on the measured Hjorringvej terrain profile shows that the prediction remains consistent with the SSPE reference and follows the measured path-loss trend.
papers.comment: Under review at IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation

papers.title: Krylov dynamics of deformed oscillator chains: localization, ballistic spreading, and indeterminacy
papers.summary: Krylov and spread complexity map quantum dynamics onto a quantum walk on a half-line whose hopping amplitudes are the Lanczos coefficients, so that Krylov dynamics is the theory of orthogonal polynomials and Jacobi operators. We use this correspondence to study Krylov chains generated by the two-parameter $(p,q)$-deformed oscillator, which interpolates between the Heisenberg--Weyl chain, the $q$-oscillator chain of double-scaled SYK, and chains with exponentially growing Lanczos coefficients. For the deformed displacement chain the spread complexity is the mean excitation number, its rate is the deformed momentum quadrature, and its acceleration is $\ddot C_K=2ω^2\langle[a,a^\dagger]\rangle$, so the deformed commutator acts as a force along the Krylov chain and the mean deformation controls early-time growth. The deformation parameters separate four regimes. For $\max(p,q)<1$ the complexity stays bounded, a localization produced by the algebra alone. For $p=1$, $q<1$ it grows ballistically, with an exact asymptotic velocity given by a theta-type series. At $p=q=1$ it grows as $t^2$. For $\max(p,q)>1$ the Jacobi operator is not essentially self-adjoint, the moment problem is indeterminate, and the Lanczos coefficients no longer determine the dynamics. Even and odd truncations converge to two different evolutions, the two reflection-symmetric N-extremal solutions of the moment problem, the odd one carrying a zero-energy atom of closed-form weight; the self-adjoint extensions yield a family of complexity curves that coincide at early times and separate once the Krylov wavefront reaches infinity. Krylov complexity in this regime is thus defined only once a boundary condition at infinite Krylov index is specified. The orthogonal-polynomial procedure and its checks on exactly solvable chains are given in the appendices.

papers.title: Model-Based Clustering of Longitudinal Functional Data with Hidden Semi-Markov Models
papers.summary: Model-based clustering of longitudinal functional data must account both for heterogeneity among curves and for temporal dependence in their latent group memberships. Functional mixture models typically treat curves as exchangeable, while temporal approaches may restrict regime persistence or ignore state-specific functional variation. We propose hidden semi-Markov models for ordered sequences of multivariate functional observations in which each latent regime has a parsimonious, state-specific functional principal subspace, extending functional high-dimensional data clustering (funHDDC) to longitudinal settings. Gaussian, contaminated-Gaussian and multivariate-$t$ emissions accommodate atypical observations, and explicit state-specific sojourn distributions govern regime persistence, with hidden Markov models as the geometric special case. Estimation uses expectation-maximization (EM) and expectation/conditional-maximization (ECM) algorithms with segmental forward-backward recursions, and identifiability is established up to label permutations and spectral indeterminacies. In simulations, temporal dependence yields the largest gains when single curves are weakly informative; with robust emissions, state-specific subspaces outperform a global functional principal component representation; and explicit durations add smaller gains when regimes overlap and sojourns are non-geometric. Applications to air-quality profiles and smartphone activity recordings, evaluated on held-out years and subjects, show improved predictive fit and illustrate how apparent duration effects can reflect time-varying transitions.

papers.title: Stellar-evolution systematic biases on $^{12}\text{C}(α,γ)^{16}\text{O}$ constraints from the primordial-black-hole mass gap
papers.summary: The $^{12}\text{C}(α,γ)^{16}\text{O}$ reaction determines helium-burning carbon-oxygen core masses and sets the pair-instability-supernova mass-gap boundary, which limits the maximum mass of stellar-origin primordial black holes. Gravitational-wave population analyses using GWTC-4 report a low-spin-black-hole upper cutoff at $68.5^{+19.8}_{-18.5}\,M_\odot$, implying a low astrophysical S-factor $S_{300}\approx 108.6\,\mathrm{keV\,barn}$, in tension with canonical nuclear-astrophysics evaluations. However, stellar-evolution systematic uncertainties from metallicity, rotation, and mass-loss prescriptions remain poorly quantified. Here we use the MESA stellar-evolution code to construct a three-dimensional parameter grid disentangling these coupled effects. We show that metallicity-dependent winds dominate helium-core retention; rotation suppresses carbon consumption via centrifugal cooling and meridional mixing; different mass-loss prescriptions produce $8$-$10\,M_\odot$ offsets in the black-hole-mass-gap edge. A parameter combination $Z\approx10^{-3}$, moderate rotation $ω/ω_\mathrm{crit}=0.4$, and optically-thin C15 winds reproduces the GWTC-4 inferred maximum primordial-black-hole mass for $S_{300}=108.6\,\mathrm{keV\,barn}$. The canonical $45\,M_\odot$ gap boundary represents an overlapping statistical intersection of black-hole-population distributions rather than a universal physical threshold. Our framework provides a pathway to jointly constrain nuclear-reaction rates, stellar-evolution physics, and gravitational-wave-source populations.

papers.title: Observation of programmable spatiotemporal quantum-inspired bits
papers.summary: Coherent superposition allows information to be encoded in the geometry of physical states1-7. Preparing individual states, however, does not determine how they can be organized throughout a wave, because the wave propagation and modulation constrain the underlying interference. Here we observe programmable spatiotemporal quantum-inspired bits in a space-time metasurface. Coherent synthesis from four discrete responses per polarization channel produces two-component states with the projective geometry of a pure quantum bit. Joint state-space synthesis retains the interference constraints of the shared waveform while allowing distinct polarization states to coexist at different resolved frequencies. Paired spatial and temporal codes organize these states into the prescribed trajectories, reconfigurable Stokes skyrmions and distinct polarizations at 48 experimentally resolved nonzero harmonic orders generated by a shared code pair. This connects the local state preparation to programmable field organization, establishing a physical basis for quantum-inspired information carriers whose encoding can exploit the geometrical paths, spatial winding and coordinated spectral states.

papers.title: CAPTA: Identifying LLMs Behind AI Agents
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agents access remote services through tools to complete user tasks, often via API calls. In this setting, a remote service may want to identify the backend LLM of an agent to launch model-specific attacks, including prompt injection or selective delivery of manipulated content. However, the service cannot directly query the backend model and must instead collect observable responses through its interactions with the agent, making identification challenging. In this paper, we present Completely Automated Preference Test to tell LLMs Apart (CAPTA), a model identification approach inspired by CAPTCHA (Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart), which distinguishes humans from automated programs. CAPTA presents multiple-choice questions as verification challenges, using differences in models' selection preferences to identify the backend LLM. It selects questions based on cross-model option-generation diversity and uses LLM-guided search to optimize their option sets. Our evaluation shows that CAPTA achieves 99.0% mean identification accuracy with only 10 questions across 25 LLMs from 10 model families. We further evaluate CAPTA with four widely used agents and seven representative LLMs, achieving 99.7% mean identification accuracy across all 28 agent-LLM combinations with 30 submitted answers.

papers.title: DeCoNav-Act: Benchmarking Collective Physical Capability in Multi-Robot Mobile Manipulation
papers.summary: Robot teams can split workloads or combine complementary bodies, but only if each robot leaves the shared world in a state its teammate can use. Existing multi-robot benchmarks emphasize task allocation and skill sequencing, rarely testing whether the resulting physical states are usable. To evaluate collective physical capability, we introduce DeCoNav-Act, a benchmark for language-guided multi-robot mobile manipulation in a shared physics simulation. Its 350 homogeneous and 150 heterogeneous tasks, each verified by joint reference execution, span two coordination mechanisms: parallel workloads in shared space and physical dependencies in which one robot establishes a condition for a teammate to use. Beyond team success, DeCoNav-Act measures path efficiency and handoff coverage and success, and adds a diagnostic from verified pre-handoff states. Evaluating sensor-grounded adaptations of ASPIRE and RAX and our agent CoMoMa, we find that with GPT-5.6-luna no method completes a task, at most 8.8% of dependencies are reached, and even from pre-handoff states no handoff is completed; with GPT-6.1-sol, CoMoMa establishes the condition in 26.5% of trials, but only 4.1% succeed.

papers.title: Probing the Rung-Mott Insulator in Bosonic Two-Leg Ladders
papers.summary: Mott insulators typically appear at integer densities, but certain lattice geometries or non-local interactions can stabilise Mott insulators at fractional densities. In this work, we study strongly interacting two-leg ladders using ultracold bosonic atoms around half-filling, and identify the rung-Mott insulating (RMI) phase through its characteristic rung occupation in site-resolved measurements. We probe its excitation spectrum via lattice modulation spectroscopy, and interpret the observed spectra using numerical simulations that include the driven dynamics, coupling to multiple excited states, and energy offsets. As with other Mott insulators, the RMI phase is characterized through its incompressibility, which we probe via a site-resolved analysis of densities and chemical potentials. Our results provide direct insight into the excitation dynamics of a strongly correlated ladder system, and pave the way for studying transport and further dynamical properties in low-dimensional quantum systems with programmable lattice geometries.

papers.title: Adaptive Multi-kernel Correntropy Kalman Filter: A Variational Bayesian Approach
papers.summary: This paper proposes an adaptive multi-kernel correntropy Kalman filter (AMCKF) for robust state estimation in the presence of heavy-tailed measurement noises and outliers. The multi-kernel correntropy loss is reformulated via half-quadratic (HQ) duality into a quadratic form with auxiliary weights, enabling efficient Kalman-like recursions. We establish a rigorous variational Bayesian framework under the mean-field assumption, deriving closed-form coordinate ascent variational inference updates for joint state and kernel width estimation. To enable online implementation, AMCKF is then proposed as an efficient single-pass approximation of the exact coordinate ascent variational inference (CAVI), where the state and auxiliary variables are updated iteratively via IRLS, followed by a closed-form kernel width update. A forgetting mechanism is designed to prevent over-confidence and ensure long-term adaptability. Simulations on target tracking and IMU attitude estimation demonstrate that the proposed AMCKF significantly outperforms standard KF, VBKF, Student's t-based KF, and fixed-kernel MKCKF in scenarios with sparse outliers, heavy-tailed noise, and mixed disturbances, while maintaining optimal performance under Gaussian conditions.

papers.title: Simultaneous Inference for Watermark Proportions in LLM-Generated Text
papers.summary: Watermarking enables detection of text generated by large language models, but practical review also requires quantifying retained signals within content of interest. Readers may choose passages based on their content and refine their selections after examining the watermark evidence. We develop simultaneous lower confidence bounds on the fraction of selected tokens that retain a watermark signal. The bounds hold jointly for the full document and any passages selected during review. We develop structure-adaptive closed testing (SACT), which uses a working model of sequential signal clustering to construct scores for calibrated sign-based tests. Under a conditional null model, the bounds have finite-sample simultaneous validity even when the working model is misspecified. An exact reference-family representation recovers the full closed-testing bounds while enabling efficient repeated queries. In a constructed database-recovery review, SACT detects document-wide watermark signals and provides lower confidence bounds on watermark proportions in selected passages. Assessing related passages together gives a sharper lower bound on their combined signal count. In simulations spanning two watermarking mechanisms and a range of signal strengths and densities, SACT generally has higher power than competing methods.

papers.title: Unbounded GHZ dimension from fixed-order multiphoton sources
papers.summary: We study the local dimension of Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states obtained by selecting events with one photon per output path. Each coherent source emits photons with a fixed internal label into a distinct set of paths, and the sets for each label partition the outputs. For two-photon sources, the maximum local dimension is 2 for every even number of paths greater than 4. However, we show that three-photon sources can produce GHZ states of arbitrarily large local dimension. To prove this, we view the three paths fed by each source as an edge of a $3$-uniform hypergraph, so that accepted emission patterns correspond exactly to perfect matchings. We construct such hypergraphs with arbitrarily many edge-disjoint perfect matchings, one per label, and no others. The construction extends to $r$-uniform hypergraphs for every fixed $r\ge3$, yielding a GHZ dimension that grows at least polynomially as the number of paths ranges over the positive multiples of $r$.

papers.title: Cosmic ray protons from 40 GeV to 10 EeV due to star formation?
papers.summary: The formation of massive stars eventually results in supernovae explosions. Typical supernova remnants (SNRs) accelerate cosmic ray (CR) protons up to $E_{max-p} \sim 10$ TeV; the value of $E_{max-p}$ may reach $\sim 1$ EeV for the case of the hypernovae and/or for a sub-relativistic velocity of the SNR's shock wave. We show that the observable CR proton spectrum in the energy range between 40 GeV and 10 EeV is reasonably well described with a sum of three components that correspond to three distinct SNR populations. We consider two basic scenarios of CR origin: I) the supergalactic scenario assuming diffusion of the protons inside a magnetic field structure with the characteristic radius $H = 1-20$ Mpc and II. the cosmological scenario with the maximum redshift of the sources $z_{max} = 6$.

papers.title: Off-axis performance characterization of hard X-ray optics for the FOXSI-4 and FOXSI-5 sounding rocket missions
papers.summary: FOXSI-4 and FOXSI-5 are Japan--U.S. joint sounding rocket missions investigating particle acceleration and plasma heating in solar flares. We developed soft and hard X-ray optics for both missions and characterized the off-axis response of the hard X-ray optics. Imaging performance was measured at SPring-8 BL29XUL, and effective areas at NASA/GSFC. With increasing off-axis angle, focused images became elongated and the large-angle component of the point spread function increased. The Half Power Diameter (HPD) remained below 20 arcsec up to 7.5 arcmin, increasing to approximately 50 arcsec at 15 arcmin. A Wolter-I optics model reproduced the off-axis HPD dependence within approximately 20%, with residuals likely associated with azimuthal variations in mirror figure errors. On-axis effective areas were 41.3 +/- 1.9 mm^2 at 6.4 keV and 32.3 +/- 1.6 mm^2 at 10 keV, decreasing by 20% and 30%, respectively, at 5 arcmin. Incorporating an empirical correction for geometric effects and X-ray reflectivity reproduced measured effective areas within 20% over 1.0--12.5 keV up to 5 arcmin. At larger off-axis angles, deviations at lower energies suggest increasing stray-light contributions. These measurements provide off-axis response data for constructing response functions for FOXSI-4 and FOXSI-5 analyses.

papers.title: DiffGR00T: Execution-Aware Differentiable Training for Humanoid Whole-Body Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have achieved strong results in arm-centric manipulation, yet humanoid whole-body control (WBC) requires dynamic balance and tightly coupled full-body coordination. Existing hierarchical humanoid VLAs typically decouple motion generation from physical execution, leaving tracking and balance errors unable to directly optimize the VLA generator. We propose DiffGR00T, an end-to-end differentiable training framework that couples GR00T N1.7 with SONIC, a pretrained whole-body behavior foundation model. To enable execution-aware differentiable training, we replace the non-differentiable simulator with a learned, action-conditioned world model, allowing multi-step body-execution losses to backpropagate through the frozen whole-body controller and the flow-matching sampler directly into the VLA action head. On four HumanoidArena simulation tasks, DiffGR00T improves average task success by 12.5 percentage points over the supervised base VLA (59.2% to 71.7%), demonstrating that execution-aware gradients effectively align high-level motion generation with closed-loop whole-body dynamics.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, 8 tables. Conference preprint. Corresponding author: Hesheng Wang

papers.title: A library-based approach for inverse reconstruction of cavity depth using angle-resolved cathodoluminescence
papers.summary: In nanofabrication processes, accurate metrology is a crucial step for obtaining control over the required critical dimensions in a device. Traditionally, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is used to obtain high resolution measurements of the lateral dimension, but obtaining depth information on a thick sample is more complex. In this work, we use angle-resolved cathodoluminescence (AR-CL) spectroscopy to resolve this third dimension. Using 30 keV electrons in the SEM, CL is created at the bottom of a micrometer scale cavity milled in a gold surface. We show that reflections of the CL off the cavity sidewalls produce an interferogram which is a sensitive probe for the cavity geometry. The interferograms can be modelled using the finite-difference time-domain method, and we demonstrate that a neural network trained on a library of these simulated patterns can be used to reconstruct the cavity depth. This approach establishes a proof of concept for AR-CL based depth reconstruction within a prescribed geometry and could form a route towards advanced three-dimensional metrology of complex nanostructures.

papers.title: Constraining the Binary Fraction and Mass-Ratio Distribution of FGK Dwarfs with Gaia XP Spectra: Metallicity, $α$-Element, and Age Dependencies
papers.summary: We present a study of the binary fraction and mass-ratio distribution for near 200,000 FGK dwarf stars within 1 kpc, utilizing the Stellar Locus Outlier (SLOT) method applied to synthetic Gaia XP photometry and stellar parameters from LAMOST DR9. By modeling the asymmetric color residuals relative to a metallicity-dependent single-star locus, we measure the binary fraction $f_b$ and constrain the power-law slope $γ_{\rm large\,q}$ of the mass-ratio distribution at high mass ratio $q$. Higher metallicity is associated with a steeper (more negative) $γ_{{\rm large}q}$, indicating a larger proportion of low-mass-ratio systems. For $α$-elements, [Mg/H] and [Si/H] are anticorrelated with $f_b$ in thin-disk-dominated subsamples; conversely, [Ca/H] shows a positive correlation with $f_b$ in thin-disk-dominated subsamples. No correlation is found between $f_b$ and $α$-element abundances in thick-disk-dominated subsamples. The binary fraction increases modestly toward older ages in the thin-disk population, a trend that likely reflects underlying correlations with chemistry. Our results shed light on how chemical composition and dynamical processes shape the binary properties of solar-type stars.
papers.comment: 24 pages, 17 figures plus 1 online figure set with 2 additional figures, 5 tables, accepted for publication in ApJ

papers.title: DexWAC: A Unified World-Actor-Critic Model for Dexterous Robot Manipulation
papers.summary: Robot demonstrations provide more than actions to imitate: they reveal how actions change the world and how those changes contribute to task success. Recent world-action models (WAMs) extend vision-language-action (VLA) models with the first signal by jointly predicting actions and future observations, yet this predictive ability serves only as an auxiliary loss for policy learning. Meanwhile, most policy improvement methods learn dynamics and values in separate models, increasing training overhead and limiting representation sharing between these complementary objectives. We introduce DexWAC, a unified world-actor-critic model that jointly learns an actor, an action-conditioned world model, and a bootstrapped critic in a single robot pretraining stage. Our key insight is that visual prediction encourages control-relevant features, while value supervision promotes task-relevant representations; together, they shape a representation suited to policy learning. Built on an image-editing backbone, DexWAC predicts, for each action chunk, the visual latent and proprioception at its endpoint together with its reward and continuation, so the world model alone efficiently yields complete imagined transitions without generating intermediate video frames. After adapting the world model and critic on real rollouts, we improve the pretrained actor through either PPO on imagined rollouts or critic-guided best-of-$N$ selection. DexWAC surpasses the large-scale pretrained VLA and WAM baselines in simulation and achieves 75% average success on two real-world tasks, compared with 45% for $π_{0.5}$. Its world model is more accurate and faster than video-based baselines, and ablations confirm that learning dynamics and value together improves the policy.

papers.title: Power Side-Channel Evaluation using Multi-FPGA Systems
papers.summary: Complex out-of-order processors are difficult to evaluate for power side-channel leakage before tapeout. A single FPGA often lacks sufficient capacity, whereas conventional CAD-based analysis is too slow to support the large numbers of traces required by practical attacks. Multi-FPGA emulation provides greater capacity, but existing partitioning schemes are not security-aware and thus results in poor attack performance. This work presents Scissors, a security-aware multi-FPGA partitioning approach for pre-silicon power side-channel evaluation of complex out-of-order processors. Scissors uses side-channel vulnerability factor (SVF) analysis to identify signals correlated with the secret key. It then keeps strongly key-correlated signals confined to one FPGA partition (measured) while moving rest of the signals to the other FPGAs (support), improving the observability of the side-channel information. We evaluate Scissors through RTL simulations and physical measurements on a two-U200 FPGA testbed, using frequency-domain CPA with a Hamming-weight leakage model. RTL ablation shows that only 68-71 high-SVF signals dominate key recovery process. For a single-core processor (SingleBOOM), Scissors recovers the key with 12,000 traces, compared with 49,000 for the unpartitioned design and 43,000 for TritonPart, while improving correct-key correlation by $2.83\times$. For a quad-core processor (QuadBOOM), which exceeds the capacity of the CW340 single-FPGA platform, Scissors reduces the required traces from 111,000 to 66,000 and improves correlation by $1.48\times$ over TritonPart. Scissors also reduces QuadBOOM RTL-to-bitstream generation from 61 h 39 min to 6 h 40 min, a $9.25\times$ speedup. These results show that security-aware partitioning improves leakage observability and attack performance while substantially reducing implementation time for complex processors against the baseline method.

papers.title: LaWanle: Why Can't Leading Driving Models Make a Simple Turn?
papers.summary: We were surprised to find that leading end-to-end driving models across major paradigms, despite scoring close to human drivers on NAVSIM, cannot reliably make a simple 90-degree turn in photorealistic closed-loop simulators. To investigate why, we build LaWanle, a benchmark of turns drawn from three such simulators. Driving each turn from several starts, we find that the same model passes it from one start and fails it from another, and that the two drives look alike until they enter the junction. Rotating the car by a few degrees at the junction entry can fail a turn it otherwise passes. Conversely, a slight heading correction to the plans can rescue about half of the failed turns we tested. Such errors arise when a model drives by itself, so we post-train an open-source lane-keeping model with closed-loop DAgger on its lateral path. Training 5% of its parameters is enough to raise its turn pass rate from 19% to 76%. The gain transfers to the two other benchmarks, where the policy also scores among the leading models. Further fine-tuning on recovery data repairs the deviations it is trained on but, against a control trained equally long, improves turns on none of the three benchmarks, and every variant stays far below a human driver.

papers.title: Neural Network Potential Reconstruction from Phase Shifts in Resonant $n+{}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ Scattering
papers.summary: We reconstruct a local, energy-independent effective potential for the narrow $D_{3/2}$ resonance of $n+{}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ from elastic phase shifts, using a Gaussian-enveloped neural parametrization coupled to a differentiable variable-phase calculation and checked by independent radial Schrödinger solvers. For the first resonance (below $2.5$ MeV LAB), the reconstruction gives a $90^\circ$ crossing at $1.001$ MeV LAB and a derivative width of $85$ keV LAB. The published Dubovichenko potential gives similar values with its original kinetic coefficient. Four reconstructions with adjustable range place the crossing within $5$ keV of one another while their central potentials span $47$ MeV. This spread illustrates the radial ambiguity of the inversion for the measured $D_{3/2}$ phases. The broad $P_{3/2}$ resonance of $n+α$ serves as a benchmark for the same method.

papers.title: Semivariance and Semivolatility in Portfolio Selection: A Unified Framework for Downside-Risk Portfolio Models
papers.summary: In this paper, we study downside risk in portfolio selection beyond minimum-risk models, where semivariance and its square root, semivolatility, yield the same portfolio. Downside-risk models are often presented as direct extensions of their variance-based counterparts, although different classes of portfolio problems require different properties of the risk measure. We classify these models by the degree of positive homogeneity of the risk measure in the weights: degree one makes risk contributions add up to the portfolio risk and keeps diversification and reward-to-risk ratios scale invariant. For three thresholds, the portfolio mean, zero and a market-index return, we state a non-degeneracy condition on long-only downside risk under which the risk-parity, most-diversified and Sortino-ratio problems are well posed. Under this condition, the two ratio problems reduce to convex programs, and the differentiability of semivolatility ensures that the risk-budgeting formulation attains the prescribed budgets. We also characterize when below-mean semivolatility is additive. Finally, we provide an out-of-sample analysis on two real-world datasets of total returns, the current constituents of the Dow Jones and Nasdaq-100 indexes. We compare seventeen long-only strategies, covering the minimum-risk, reward-to-risk, risk-parity and most-diversified families, in a rolling-window backtest, and test the differences within each family by block-bootstrap inference.

papers.title: Critical Eddington luminosity and photon cooling of compact spherical stars
papers.summary: Context. Relativistic corrections to the luminosity have been used for neutron stars of radius greater than $3MG/c^2$ in studies of X-ray bursts. However, there is no fundamental limit that excludes the existence of more compact massive objects with a physical surface, fluid or solid. Aims. We aim to discuss critical "Eddington" luminosity for spherical stars that have a surface within the sphere of unstable circular photon orbits (photon sphere). Methods. We use standard analytical ray-tracing formulae in the Schwarzschild metric. Results. We find that for stars within the photon sphere, the Eddington condition for balance between radiative force and gravitational attraction is fundamentally altered by photons returning to the surface. The equilibrium is non-local and requires stationarity on timescales of photon fall-back. As a result, spontaneous symmetry breaking is possible, leading to non-uniformity of emission across the photospheric surface. Conclusions. For a fixed intrinsic luminosity, the photons returning to the surface decrease the cooling rate of stars inside their photon sphere. At the same time, the returning photons increase the value of the critical luminosity that would balance gravity. One and the same redshifted formula applies to the critical luminosity, as seen by a distant observer, for any radius of the star. In the X-ray burst literature, for stars with radius less than 3 gravitational radii a different formula has long been accepted that missed the essential physics of the photons emitted in directions outside the escape cone.

papers.title: Electrons in a hard-wall cylinder with helicoidal metric: time-reversal pairing, cubic anticrossings, and twist-activated dipole transitions
papers.summary: We study the scalar Schrödinger equation in a helicoidal metric when the axial direction is closed by Dirichlet walls built into the operator domain. With hard walls, the axial derivative cannot be replaced by a traveling-wave factor, and in a rotationally symmetric spinless cavity, time reversal makes the levels with azimuthal numbers $m$ and $-m$ exactly degenerate. We write the Hamiltonian as a Hermitian coupled-subband matrix and give an exact gauge-adapted variational representation. For a finite radius, the leading twist correction is quadratic, and changes sign at a critical aspect ratio; for an unbounded radial domain, it is linear in $|Ω_g|$. Retuning the aspect ratio through an isolated radial--axial resonance within one $m$ sector opens an avoided crossing with gap $Δ_{\mathrm{gap}}/E_R=1.648775\ldots|Ω_gR^2/L|^3$ to leading order. A transverse dipole transition forbidden without twist acquires an oscillator strength quadratic in the twist, with leading coefficient $0.0559408010$ for $R/L=2$ from perturbation theory. Dipole sum rules and the convergence of the currents serve as checks on the numerics. We also give the inverse-mass tensor required for a scalar realization and re-examine each statement and figure of the earlier article [Opt. Quantum Electron. \textbf{58}, 113 (2026)] within the corrected model.
papers.comment: 26 pages, 17 figures, 8 tables. Corrects the analysis of E. O. Silva, Opt. Quantum Electron. 58, 113 (2026), doi:10.1007/s11082-026-08693-8, whose retraction has been requested. Scripts and verification tests are provided as ancillary files

papers.title: Partial Identification under Imperfect Compliance via Cross-World Correlation Restriction
papers.summary: This article develops a unified partial identification approach for the average treatment effect (ATE) and the local average treatment effect (LATE) in randomized experiments with imperfect compliance, incorporating the cross-world correlation between potential treatment statuses. Even under random assignment and exclusion restriction, the correlation is unidentified. However, given the two identified marginals, it uniquely determines the relative proportions of the four principal strata, with monotonicity corresponding to a special case. We derive explicit sharp bounds for both the ATE and LATE at a fixed correlation and extend the results to prespecified correlation ranges, providing a sensitivity analysis that incorporates substantive information about compliance behavior. For the ATE, the lower bound decreases and the upper bound increases with the correlation. Although imposing monotonicity does not tighten the conventional Balke--Pearl bounds, we show that restricting the correlation can yield tighter bounds, even when defiers remain possible. For the LATE, the sharp bounds may not vary monotonically with the correlation, and we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for point identification of the LATE at any feasible correlation value, with the conventional Wald ratio identification result under monotonicity as a special case. In addition, we derive a breakdown point for the correlation that determines when the Wald ratio falls outside the sharp identified set for the LATE. Applications to four empirical studies illustrate how cross-world correlation restrictions tighten the sharp bounds for the ATE and LATE and assess the breakdown of the Wald ratio.

papers.title: Inflation at strong mixing as a connection problem: effective field theory, Stokes phenomenon and the cosmological collider
papers.summary: We study a massive field strongly mixed with the curvature perturbation during inflation, in the regime where the latter is described at low energies by a single-field effective field theory (EFT) with a quadratic dispersion relation. What this EFT captures, and what lies beyond it, are encoded in a connection problem, which relates the solutions that define the vacuum at early times to those that describe observables at late times. We solve it with a general method that does not rely on an exact solution. An expansion in the inverse mixing, keeping both fields, yields the EFT as its leading order, with corrections under systematic control. It selects the vacuum of the EFT, fixes a phase that the EFT cannot determine on its own, and describes the heavy mode at all times. Particle production lies beyond all orders of this asymptotic expansion. We show that it arises from a Stokes phenomenon at the complex branch points of the dispersion relation and that, in a rotating basis of the two fields, it reduces to the familiar production of particles with half the heavy mass. A reflection symmetry of the equations of motion, combined with the canonical commutation relations, then determines all exponentially small effects exactly, and with them the solution of the connection problem, which combines particle production with a conversion between light and heavy quanta. Together with the expansion, these exact results give a compact analytical formula for the cosmological collider signal, whose exponential suppression, half of the usual Boltzmann one, directly reflects the halved mass of the produced particles. The expansion only requires a separation of scales and the adiabaticity of the heavy mode, while the reflection symmetry holds for many systems in de Sitter space. We therefore expect this approach to bring physical understanding and simple formulas well beyond the present case.

papers.title: Modulations of the photoswitching performances of azobenzene-based molecular devices by the π-conjugated spacers
papers.summary: The nature of the π-conjugated spacer is a key element to tune the electrical conductance and optical switching properties of metal-spacer-azobenzene-metal molecular devices. We report that the azobenzene-based molecular junctions with a thiophene or a phenylthiophene spacer exhibit a high cis/trans conductance ratio (ca. 1,000), while those with a bithiophene spacer have a lower conductance switching ratio (ca. 500) at the stated conditions (light wavelength and intensity) and for one batch of samples (out of two). Similarly, the two former molecular junctions have quite similar trans-to-cis isomerization kinetics, while the latter has a lower switching rate. The energy level of the highest occupied molecular orbital, which controls the electron transfer in the molecular junction, is weakly influenced by the nature of the spacer, nor by the conformation of the azobenzene moieties. The large increase in the conductance of the molecular junction with azobenzene in the cis-state is explained by an increase in the electronic coupling energy between the molecule and the top electrode. Theoretical studies by Density Functional Theory and Non Equilibrium Green's Functions are qualitatively consistent with the experiments. We find a consistent structure-property trend, showing that the higher molecule/electrode coupling energy for the cis-state is explained by the top benzene ring of the azobenzene lying flat with respect to the top electrode for the thiophene, phenylthiophene and bithiophene spacers. On the contrary, we observe that a spacer with a carbon-carbon triple bond (acetylene thiophene) induces a large irreproducibility and unpredictability of the results.

papers.title: Privacy Disclosure Control Benchmark (PDC-Bench): How Faithfully Do LLMs Keep Privacy Constraints on In-Context Disclosure Granularity?
papers.summary: In LLM task execution, a constraint on the permitted disclosure granularity of personal attributes is sometimes imposed on the output. For example, if a person's private attribute is their location (San Francisco) and disclosure is permitted only at the country level, an output at the state level (California) violates the constraint. Detecting such violations requires capturing not only direct privacy leakage (San Francisco) but also semantic leakage (California). However, existing benchmarks cannot measure the degree of leakage with respect to a given semantic constraint such as the country-level limit. We therefore formalize disclosure control as a constraint on the permitted ceiling over the hierarchy of a knowledge graph. Building on this formulation, we construct PDC-Bench, a benchmark of 16,105 samples covering geography, age, race and ethnicity, and occupation. In our experiments applying PDC-Bench to eleven LLMs, 62% of the constraint violations were semantic leakage. We further found that semantic leakage depends less on the model than on the permitted disclosure granularity and the task's need for the private attribute; reliable auditing must therefore target semantic leakage together with these two factors. Data, prompts, and code are available at https://github.com/fuji1655/PDC-Bench.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of complex crystals from a generalized mean-field bond model
papers.summary: We extend our previously introduced mean-field bond model from unary fcc lattices to crystals with multiple chemical species and sublattices, accurately predicting finite-temperature thermodynamics without statistical sampling. Our generalization reformulates the model in terms of the Wyckoff positions of the crystal, representing each by one atom, and solving for the bond density of the reference bond of each of its neighbor shells. Bond-bond correlation functions are built from the zero-temperature force constants, allowing the deviation of every bond in the crystal to be expressed through linear functions of the reference bond of a shell. Thermodynamic self-consistency is enforced by requiring a single virial temperature for the whole crystal, and compatibility of average bond lengths with crystal volume. Model predictions are validated against molecular dynamics simulations of unary, binary, and ternary crystals using Morse-type bonding potentials, parametrized for each shell from the force constants of empirical interatomic potentials at several isotropic strains. In each case, the predicted bond densities and thermodynamics agree with the simulations to within their statistical uncertainty. We discuss strategies for combining the model with bonding potentials parametrized from first principles and foundation models to predict the finite-temperature thermodynamics of complex crystals at ab initio accuracy without statistical sampling.
papers.comment: 16 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Code: https://github.com/raynol-dsouza/mean-field-bond-model (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24493341). Data: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24466123

papers.title: Total kinetic energy of fission fragments within time-dependent density functional theory: role of particle-number projection and collective deformations
papers.summary: Time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations of fission fragment total kinetic energy (TKE), restricted to axially symmetric trajectories and a single symmetry-violating mean-field state, underestimate TKE by 10-20 MeV away from the most probable mass split. We reexamine this for $^{240}$Pu and $^{252}$Cf within relativistic TDDFT+BCS, combining particle-number projection (PNP) with an extended collective space including hexadecapole and non-axial deformations. Varying the pairing strength leaves the TKE essentially unchanged, but PNP converts each trajectory into a resolved TKE distribution over fragment mass, and the enlarged collective space is needed to reach the correct scission configurations. Together, these reproduce the empirical TKE mass dependence substantially better than standard calculations, indicating the discrepancy reflects missing symmetry restoration and configuration space rather than a deficient energy functional.

papers.title: Emergent cloud patterns from stochastic jump models of parcel microphysics
papers.summary: Warm clouds organize into bands, cells, and intricate wave networks, yet the dynamical mechanisms connecting these forms remain difficult to isolate. To bridge unresolved parcel microphysics and cloud organization, we formulate a spatial jump-process model of cloud-water and rain-water anomalies in an activated regime and analyze its mean-field closure. Eliminating fast supersaturation adjustment from droplet growth and vapor transport supplies a screened environmental kernel, which we couple to a cubic Stuart-Landau oscillatory law. Averaging over Poisson parcel episodes and closing third-order moments yields a pseudoparabolic Ginzburg--Landau equation (PGLE), whose mixed space--time derivative encodes dynamic inertia, slowing fine-scale relaxation. Unlike diffusive amplitude equations, the PGLE splits into a regularized nonlinear Schrödinger Hamiltonian sector and a pseudoparabolic Allen--Cahn gradient sector governed by a conserved Noether charge, alongside an open-system liquid-water budget separating conversion from vapor exchange, fallout, and triad-driven domain-mean oscillations. Exact stability criteria show how dynamic inertia and amplitude-dependent frequency shifts (twist) control modulational loss of synchrony and resonant cross-carrier sideband gain above a critical twist threshold. Numerical integrations show that increasing twist transforms undulatus-like bands into defect-rich asperitas-like waves via defect proliferation, while subcritical competition consolidates cellular patterns into rolls. Even without twist, random anomalies evolve into a persistent cellular exclusion scale and actinoform-like spiral arms, while 1D wave breakup reorganizes into a two-frequency combination-tone spectrum. The jump model identifies omitted fluctuation moments for calibration against large-eddy simulations.

papers.title: Perfect Scores, Misplaced Explanations: A Controlled Study of Explainability in Audio Deepfake Detection
papers.summary: What if an explanation achieves perfect scores but it is uninterpretable? We show that this happens when explaining audio deepfake detectors. Using an optimization-based method, we explain a state-of-the-art wav2vec2-based detector. The explanations achieve optimal scores on standard explainability metrics, i.e. fidelity and faithfulness. Visual inspection, however, reveals unintuitive and uninterpretable patterns. To understand this discrepancy, we run a controlled perturbation study in which we modify known frequency regions of the speech signal. Although we propose a model that is able to obtain close-to-optimal results with respect to the metrics, the explanations locate the manipulated region only when it is fixed across samples, and mostly fall to chance level when it varies. We further show that the signal used to fill the removed regions largely determines the explanation and its localization, without being reflected in the metrics.
papers.comment: Submitted to ICASSP worshop on Explainability, Robustness, and Controllability of Language Modeling for Speech and Audio

papers.title: A consistent generalised kinetic equation for damped ocean waves
papers.summary: Contemporary spectral wave models, including those used in operational wave forecasts and in coupled earth system models, assume damping and non-linear wave energy exchange to be independent. Here, we critically examine this assumption. Starting from the equations of weakly non-linear waves, we rigorously derive a governing equation that consistently couples damping and non-linear interactions. This consistent generalised kinetic equation does not lead to an appreciable change in total wave--energy dissipation, but compared to the standard additive damping approach there is a noticeable difference in the distribution of energy among the wave frequencies. This effect is particularly important for weak damping, and is a consequence of a memory effect retained in model. Even stronger differences are observed when damping is allowed to depend on wave frequency, as is characteristic of many wave processes of growing interest such as the interaction with other components of the earth system, e.g. the cryosphere. Compared to the purely additive formulation, our new damped generalised kinetic equation has improved numerical stability characteristics. The formulation presented therefore provides a possible basis for future operational wave modelling. While our results are for ocean waves, the derived generalised kinetic equation can be applied to other weakly nonlinear dispersive systems where external damping (or forcing) applies.

papers.title: Topological terahertz fields from tunable vectorial currents
papers.summary: Future information processing calls for photonic architectures with greater capacity, intrinsic resilience to noise, and direct integration with quantum materials and devices. Topological light pulses have recently emerged as promising candidates to meet these demands, yet the complexity underlying their unique properties also makes them challenging to generate, tune, and fully resolve in space and time. Here, we generate and actively tune topological light fields through transient vectorial currents in an optoelectronic metasurface. Incident linear polarization steers the local direction of photocurrents in graphene via nanoplasmonic resonators with triangular symmetry, while a global winding pattern enables continuous tuning between compressional and circulating charge flows. Under ultrafast excitation, these currents radiate single-cycle terahertz toroidal pulses spanning electric- and magnetic-dominant modes with dynamically evolving skyrmion textures. Full spatiotemporal mapping and reconstruction provide a complete visualization of the toroidal structure of light, directly tracing the closed field surfaces while continuously tracking skyrmion number and helicity throughout a single cycle. These results connect two-dimensional vectorial currents to rich three-dimensional electromagnetic field structures, while establishing a versatile integrated platform for higher-dimensional photonic information processing and emerging material spectroscopies.

papers.title: Witnessing Gaussian Coexistence and Correlation-Ellipse Tomography
papers.summary: Gaussian light is specified by second-order field moments, yet their hidden correlation geometry can demand higher-order intensity measurements. We establish a measurement hierarchy for "Gaussian coexistence", i.e., the simultaneous presence of cross covariance and cross pseudocovariance. For two zero-mean Gaussian modes with circular marginals, all unperturbed intensity moments of second or third order are blind to coexistence. In contrast, a balanced fourth-order residual provides a necessary and sufficient witness. Their identities, however, remain fundamentally ambiguous: recovering the two correlation strengths does not reveal which belongs to the covariance and which to the pseudocovariance. Unexpectedly, adding thermal fluctuations resolves this ambiguity: an independent, correlated thermal probe selectively modifies the covariance while leaving the pseudocovariance unchanged, allowing the two correlation strengths to be individually identified. Moreover, a coherent reference in only one arm then makes their relative phase accessible through third-order intensity correlation. Together, these measurements reconstruct a correlation ellipse and its Poincaré-sphere coordinates, determining the relative channel strengths and the ellipse orientation. The framework separates what intensity detection can witness, what thermal probing can identify, and what a single phase reference can orient, turning inaccessible Gaussian correlation structure into a quantitatively reconstructible geometry.

papers.title: Analytic response functions of space-based gravitational-wave detectors to ultralight scalar-field dark matter under multiple types of TDI combinations
papers.summary: Ultralight scalar fields are important candidates for dark matter. As coherently oscillating fields, they can leave characteristic signatures in space-based gravitational-wave detectors through their coupling to test masses. In this paper, we derive analytic expressions for the response functions of space-based gravitational-wave detectors to ultralight scalar-field dark matter under multiple types of time-delay interferometry (TDI) combinations. Starting from the coupling action between the scalar field and a test mass, we obtain the additional displacement of the test mass and the single-link Doppler response. We then give the general analytic form of the response function for an arbitrary TDI combination and compare the analytic and Monte Carlo numerical results for the optimal combinations A, E, and T. Finally, we analyze the responses of multiple types of TDI combinations, classify them into ordinary and ζ types according to their low-frequency behavior, and give the low-frequency response expressions of the individual combinations. The results can be used to evaluate the sensitivity of space-based gravitational-wave missions such as LISA, Taiji, and TianQin to the mass and coupling parameters of ultralight scalar-field dark matter.

papers.title: Automated Design and Evaluation Pipeline for Optimal Control Transcriptions in Model Predictive Control
papers.summary: The computational burden of Model Predictive Control represents a bottleneck limiting its widespread deployment in real-time applications. The selection of the optimal control transcription strategy for a given MPC formulation is a key driver of computational efficiency. Identifying performant MPC transcriptions requires significant effort and domain knowledge. We propose an automated pipeline for the design and evaluation of performant optimal control transcriptions for a given MPC formulation. Custom multi-objective design metrics, such as computation time or closed-loop performance, can be specified and are minimized by the pipeline. As a transcription method, a pseudospectral Legendre-Gauss-Radau method is employed. We show that it incorporates forward Euler integration and implicit collocation methods of low and high order in one formulation, leveraging the pipeline to evaluate both numerical approaches. Furthermore, different mesh configurations can be parameterized. To identify the optimal configuration of the transcription, a Bayesian Optimization framework is applied. The pipelines improvements in MPC performance are demonstrated through On-Orbit Servicing scenarios involving spacecraft motion planning and closed-loop control.

papers.title: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Forward Scatter Radar
papers.summary: Forward Scatter Radar (FSR) enhances the detection of low-observable targets by exploiting the increased radar cross section that occurs when a target crosses the transmitter-receiver baseline. Conventional FSR typically uses single-input single-output (SISO) architectures with limited localization capability, while recent single-input multiple-output (SIMO) systems enable non-coherent angular estimation. This paper introduces a multiple-input multiple-output FSR (MIMO-FSR) framework for joint estimation of target direction of departure (DoD) and direction of arrival (DoA) from non-coherent, amplitude-only measurements. By exploiting antenna arrays at both the transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX), the proposed approach enables two-dimensional angular localization without phase synchronization among TX/RX array elements. We establish the underlying operating principle under ideal signal separability and then develop practical frequency-division multiplexing (FDM) and time-division multiplexing (TDM) implementations. For each scheme, dedicated signal models and processing methods compensate for distortions caused by frequency offsets and target motion, respectively. We also derive analytical expressions for angular resolution, ambiguity conditions, and output-map distortions. Extensive numerical simulations for short- and long-baseline scenarios reveal operational limits and trade-offs between the two multiplexing schemes. Finally, proof-of-concept outdoor experiments using software-defined radio platforms validate the proposed framework. The results demonstrate joint DoD-DoA estimation and support the feasibility of MIMO-FSR for future active, passive, and integrated sensing and communications applications.

papers.title: Softer charged-hadron spectra in Ne+Ne than in O+O collisions at the same multiplicity at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV
papers.summary: Charged-hadron spectra measured by the ATLAS Collaboration in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV are compared at the same charged-particle multiplicity instead of at the same centrality, to test whether the shape of the transverse-momentum spectrum at a given multiplicity depends on the size of the colliding system. At equal multiplicity, Ne+Ne collisions have a lower mean transverse momentum $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ than O+O collisions. Without any spectral fit, the published $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ values give a Ne+Ne/O+O ratio of 0.9822 at 3-4% centrality, 6.6 standard deviations below unity even if the O+O systematic uncertainties are taken as uncorrelated between centrality classes. At $0.4 < p_{\rm T} < 2$ GeV the Ne+Ne spectrum is described by the O+O spectrum with the transverse-momentum axis compressed by a single stretch factor, $λ_{\rm Ne/O} = 0.969$ in the 3-4% class. It lies 9.5 or 3.3 standard deviations below unity, depending on whether the common part of the O+O systematic uncertainties cancels between centrality classes. This ordering is expected if Ne+Ne collisions have a larger transverse area at the same multiplicity and a larger area gives a softer spectrum. The softening decreases towards peripheral collisions and is the same at forward pseudorapidity. In central collisions the spectral shape follows the centrality class more closely than the multiplicity. The same procedure is tested in Xe+Xe and Pb+Pb collisions.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables; submitted to Phys. Rev. C

papers.title: Waveform Randomization for Secure ISAC Against Informed Eavesdroppers
papers.summary: We study waveform-level protection of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) against a UAV-mounted eavesdropper (Eve) that knows the waveform construction and the phase-key generation rules. The novelty of this work is a systematic, budget-explicit attack analysis: instead of relying on undisclosed design details, we quantify what an informed Eve can learn and reconstruct, and how much computation this takes. We protect the sensing reference with Fourier-curve modulation, phase keys, and tangent Artificial Noise (AN), with burst- specific information shared over secure backhaul. We compare three key-generation rules against offline Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based sequence identification and online Adam and phase-aware expectation-maximization (EM) key recovery, under complete or partial nominal-sequence knowledge. A power- domain model couples residual key error with imperfect AN removal and predicts coherent delay locking. Results show that reusable key structure permits sequence identification even when demodulation fails, position-dependent keying raises recovery difficulty, and seed-expanded keying resists the evaluated clas- sifier within the learning budget. Waveform simulations under multipath, clutter, and echo accumulation confirm the sensing impact.
papers.comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Communication

papers.title: Analyzing Single-Bit Flips on LLMs and Their Backbone-Matched VLMs
papers.summary: Open-weight large language models (LLMs) enable offline weight analysis and are reused as backbones in vision-language models (VLMs), increasing the risk of bit-flip attacks that manipulate stored weight bits to induce malicious model behavior. An adversary could identify vulnerable bits on a public LLM and later flip the same locations in a deployed LLM or its backbone-matched VLMs. A single-bit flip is particularly practical in this setting because it is easier to achieve under hardware fault attacks than multi-bit flips. However, existing selectors are mostly limited to multi-bit flips, without in-depth analysis of single-bit flips. In this paper, we adapt representative data-free and data-based bit selectors to identify candidate bits. We evaluate each bit independently on source LLMs and at the same logical coordinates in backbone-matched VLMs (without re-search), considering both performance degradation and prediction patterns across multiple inputs. Results show impact of single-bit flips varies across selectors on LLMs and their backbone-matched VLMs. A single-bit flip can make the model tend to produce a repeated output string across different inputs. Our robustness analysis reveals vulnerabilities in terms of performance and prediction patterns.

papers.title: Dynamic stochastic multi-attribute group decision-making based on fractional-order stochastic dominance criteria
papers.summary: The stochastic dominance criterion has been widely employed in stochastic multi-attribute decision making as a robust tool for quantitatively comparing decision-makers' preferences over alternatives. Existing research predominantly relies on integer-order stochastic dominance criteria within static modeling frameworks. However, the integer-order scale is often too coarse, and real-world decision-making typically occurs in dynamic environments, for which static methods are inadequate. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel dynamic stochastic multi-attribute group decision making model based on fractional-order stochastic dominance criteria. In this model, we introduce the priority degree under fractional-order stochastic dominance, which not only encompasses the priority degree under integer-order stochastic dominance, but also is applicable to decision-makers whose utility functions are not concave everywhere. Consequently, the proposed model captures the dominance relations between alternatives with greater accuracy and flexibility. Moreover, the model allows for the addition or removal of attributes and alternatives across decision periods, thereby exhibiting the applicability to any dynamic decision process. Numerical examples and comparative analyses show the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach, highlighting its broader applicability compared with conventional methods. This study enriches the theoretical foundation of dynamic stochastic multi-attribute group decision making and contributes to improving the reliability and precision of decision outcomes.
