As AI systems become increasingly capable of performing human-level work they may be deployed to tasks that people find enjoyable while simultaneously creating comparatively more aversive tasks such as monitoring AI outputs. This creates a thorny tradeoff for managers: whether work should be assigned purely based on the expected performance of the workers in question, or also account for the subjective experience of the person potentially doing the task. Most economic accounts focus on expected utility calculations based on the former. Here, we assess how people balance objective outcomes and more subjective qualities like enjoyment. In a series of large-scale (N=800) behavioral studies in which people allocate tasks to either an AI or human worker we find that people's allocation decisions are best captured by a model that systematically balances relative objective performance with the human worker's expected enjoyment, weighting human experience higher when a task is framed as inducing less enjoyment and adjusting based on the stakes of the task. As AI also makes decisions about work allocation, we compare a set of LLMs. We find many models also deviate from purely objective decisions, particularly when the project stakes are low, but there is wide heterogeneity as to how much and in what manner they weigh enjoyment. These results raise questions about what role human experience may play in decisions around where and how to integrate AI into workplaces. Integration may be jagged across settings due to consideration not only of the relative capabilities of workers, but also the human experience of work, the valence of that experience (e.g., more strongly weighing aversion), the context (e.g., stakes), and who is making or guiding such choices (human or LLM).

papers.title: AI-Assisted Programming and Labor Demand
papers.summary: Generative AI has demonstrated human-level performance on technical work tasks, yet evidence on how these task-level capabilities are changing labor demand remains scarce. We study the firm-level adoption of GitHub Copilot, an AI coding assistant, across 5,414 multinational firms accounting for 38% of the U.S. programming workforce. To identify causal effects, we exploit a natural experiment generated by firms' predetermined software procurement cycles. Early AI-adopting firms hired more workers before the launch of GitHub Copilot and had larger, more technical, and older workforces. After one year, GitHub Copilot adoption reduces quarterly technical hiring by 29% among review-induced adopters, with no effect on separations, overall technical headcount, or vacancy duration. The hiring slowdown is concentrated in the subset of junior technical roles that involve the highest share of coding work. Overall, AI coding assistance causes firms to shift demand towards more experienced workers and roles that pair some coding with broader design responsibilities.

papers.title: Finite Temperature Isoscalar Instabilities and Moat Regimes in Relativistic Nuclear Matter
papers.summary: We study the finite-temperature isoscalar collective response of symmetric nuclear matter in three relativistic mean-field descriptions: the linear Walecka model, its nonlinear extension, and the quark-meson coupling (QMC) model. The Walecka models are formulated in terms of nucle- onic degrees of freedom, whereas QMC incorporates quark degrees of freedom confined inside the nucleon. These models differ in their treatment of scalar interactions at finite density, affecting instability boundaries. Focusing on the coupled scalar-vector channel, we track how the boundaries of homogeneous instabilities evolve with temperature. In all three models, we find a nonmonotonic momentum dependence of the static response, characterized by a minimum at finite momentum, a moat regime that selects a preferred length scale for density fluctuations. Our results show that this moat structure is robust against thermal effects across these relativistic nuclear matter models, providing motivation for future studies of inhomogeneous phases in hot and dense astrophysical matter.

papers.title: Spurious Information in Large Markets: Random Matrix Laws for Entropy, Mutual Information and the Value of Information
papers.summary: Entropy, Kullback-Leibler divergence and mutual information have become standard currencies for measuring how much one set of financial variables reveals about another. In large cross-sections they are almost always computed from sample covariance matrices, and the noise in those matrices is the object of random matrix theory. This paper develops the random matrix theory of Gaussian information functionals and applies it to markets. I show that the plug-in mutual information between two blocks of p and r variables estimated from $n$ observations has an exact expected excess, the spurious information, that is a digamma telescope independent of the true dependence. Under independence its law is that of a product of Beta variables. In the proportional regime it grows linearly with an order-one variance. The same quantity is a linear spectral statistic of the Jacobi ensemble, which yields a closed form for the logarithmic moment of Wachter's law. Spurious information increases strictly whenever uninformative coordinates are added. In a CARA-Gaussian economy the certainty-equivalent value of a signal equals mutual information divided by risk aversion, so these results translate one for one into a spurious value of information. The canonical-correlation phase transition then defines a frontier of minimum detectable information. On daily returns of 49 US industry portfolios from 1990 to 2026, I document the market mode, the reliability of sector eigenvectors implied by the BBP transition, the out-of-sample cost of noise dressing, and an information linkage between carbon-intensive and financial industries that survives exact bias correction and conditioning on the market.

papers.title: Design an Algorithmic Stablecoin based on a Predictive PID Controller
papers.summary: Cryptocurrencies issued based on blockchain technology have attracted increasing attention in recent years. However, their high volatility makes it difficult for them to become circulating currencies. This led to the creation of stablecoins. Existing stablecoins can be divided into three main categories: stablecoins pegged to fiat currencies, stablecoins collateralized by crypto assets, and algorithmically controlled stablecoins. Most existing stablecoins are either of the first two types. We design an algorithmic stablecoin controlled only by a predictive Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller, which uses the price forecasted by Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model as part of its input. Simulation experiments show that, under ideal market conditions, the stablecoin can achieve long-term goals that fluctuate within a pre-defined range. Furthermore, it consistently restores prices to the anchor interval in the presence of exogenous disturbances.

papers.title: Robust bounds for American fixed-strike lookback puts
papers.summary: We initiate the robust (model-independent) pricing of American lookback options under martingale optimal transport (MOT) constraints. Given finitely many marginals of the discounted price, we study the maximal expected discounted payoff of an American fixed-strike lookback put, whose exercise value at $t$ is $(K-\min_{u\le t}e^{ru}X_u)^+$, i.e.\ a function of the running minimum $m_t$ of the undiscounted price. Two structural facts isolate this as the non-trivial American lookback problem: at $r=0$ every classical lookback degenerates to its European counterpart, while at $r>0$ the max-based fixed-strike lookback call remains European-type, but the min-based put is genuinely American. We prove a pricing--hedging duality using the continuous-time duality of Guo--Obłoj and reducing the hedge to the two-dimensional state $(X_t,m_t)$. In the two-period model, we establish a convexity lemma and exact decomposition of the continuation payoff, deriving the exercise criterion and closed-form free-continuation value. The optimal continuation coupling is the monotone martingale coupling (the third extremal coupling), and we show that the optimal exercise region is a right tail $\{x\ge x^*\}$, in sharp contrast to the left-tail region of the standard American put. The threshold $x^*$ is monotone in parameters and affine in $K$. For finitely many marginals, the structure extends unconditionally: the optimal exercise region is always a right tail, and the optimal coupling is the reflected iterated Azéma--Yor embedding, minimizing the running minimum in stochastic order. Under the reflected Obłoj--Spoida assumption, this embedding is a two-point iterated monotone coupling; otherwise, it includes a local mass-diffusion correction. We quantify the American and model-risk premia.

papers.title: Diffractive Photoproduction of High $p_T$ Photons in Ultraperipheral Collisions at the LHC
papers.summary: We investigate diffractive photoproduction of large-transverse-momentum photons in ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC, considering different collision systems and alternative descriptions of the BFKL Pomeron. We estimate cross sections and differential distributions including NLO corrections to the BFKL characteristic function and assess the prospects for measuring this process in ultraperipheral pp, pPb, and PbPb collisions. We find that the cross sections are sizable, and that future measurements in this channel can help constrain BFKL dynamics and improve our understanding of high-energy QCD.

papers.title: Toward the Centennial of Wigner's Supermultiplet Symmetry: an Ab Initio Perspective
papers.summary: As the centennial of Wigner's supermultiplet theory approaches in 2037, this review offers a modern perspective through the recently advanced ab initio Symmetry Adapted Model (SAM). We begin with the symmetry's empirical foundations in two-nucleon data and electroweak processes, and trace its emergence from the strong force through effective field theories, the QCD large-$N_c$ limit, the similarity renormalization group, and lattice calculations. We then follow its historical arc, from early limited engagement, through its revived interest, to the modern algebraic and first-principles resurgence. Central to this renaissance are new nullspace-based algorithms for the U(3) and U(4) coupling and recoupling coefficients, which remove a bottleneck spanning nearly nine decades and are released as the open-source libraries u3lib and u4lib. Building on them, the SAM is the first large-scale ab initio shell model to encode both Elliott's spatial U(3) and Wigner's spin-isospin U(4) symmetries, resolving individual supermultiplets that share the same quadratic Casimir eigenvalue. Early results show that the spin-isospin symmetry strongly dominates high-fidelity chiral interactions and suppresses spin-isospin polarizability in light nuclei. We close with potential directions that the SAM is poised to advance within the next decade.

papers.title: LeCellModel: Interpretable Density Estimation over the Gene Expression Manifold
papers.summary: Representation learning for single-cell RNA-seq has been evaluated by the identities representations capture -- cell types, lineages, perturbations -- rather than how faithfully they model the distribution of cell states on the gene expression manifold. As a result, density estimation, rare-state detection, perturbation scoring, and gene-level attribution are bolted onto frozen embeddings as separate models, disconnected from the geometry of the data. We argue that modeling the distribution of cell states should be the primary objective, and that representation quality follows from it. Building on LeJEPA, whose SIGReg objective enforces a provably optimal isotropic Gaussian latent, we introduce LeCellModel, which reads the encoder's Jacobian log-volume (JEPA-SCORE) under this Gaussian latent as a relative typicality score. Across several datasets, LeCellModel outperforms established methods on the scIB benchmark for representation quality. Furthermore, we show that LeCellModel enables detection of rare expression states using JEPA-SCORE as a typicality measure, applying it to a controlled cytokine panel, where it identifies stimulated cells across minority fractions and tracks pathway-response magnitude. We introduce gene-level interpretability of the typicality score -- to our knowledge, the first method for analyzing JEPA-SCORE in feature space. Leveraging this framework, LeCellModel recapitulates the known association of a profibrotic macrophage program with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and discovers a CD177+ activated regulatory T cell subpopulation previously described only in tumor contexts. Both findings emerge directly from the geometry of the learned embedding, without relying on supervised annotations.

papers.title: Emergence of collectivity in the $0^+_2$ band of $^{92}$Zr
papers.summary: The $2^+_2 \rightarrow 0^+_2$ transition in $^{92}$Zr was observed for the first time in a high-statistics decay study of the 10-day isomer $^{92m}$Nb. Its $E2$ transition strength of 8.9(7) W.u. is enhanced by 40% relative to the ground state band, providing evidence for a collective structure built on the $0^+_2$ state which is analogous to the deformed shape-coexisting configuration in $^{94}$Zr.

papers.title: Big Tree Viewer: A high-performance browser-based phylogenetic tree viewer with agentic AI integration
papers.summary: Phylogenetic trees represent evolutionary history visually, and the ability to display and explore them is a key function in research across biological disciplines. Very large gene and species trees are becoming common with the increasing availability of low cost DNA sequencing, creating performance and informativeness challenges for display software originally designed for phylogenies with a few hundred to a few thousand tips. We discuss these limitations and introduce a browser-based Big Tree Viewer (BTV) highly optimized for fast display and biologically informative exploration of phylogenetic trees containing even a million tips. BTV can automatically map binomial species names to the NCBI or Catalogue of Life taxonomies and display colored ribbons to indicate taxonomic groups for enhanced exploration. Even without taxonomic mapping, BTV automatically labels groups of neighboring tips that share the first word of their names, such as a genus or gene family name, providing readable large-scale landmarks when individual tip labels are too dense to read. BTV supports metadata display, visual customization, tanglegram-like tree comparisons, statistics, figure export, and multiple tree layouts, including a new spiral form to display enormously large trees. BTV is also designed to integrate with common agentic AI tools, allowing agents to display, style, annotate, and inspect trees at the user's request. The BTV web app is freely available at https://BigTreeViewer.net and runs entirely in the user's browser, with no data uploads to any central server. Desktop versions of the BTV app for macOS, Windows, and Linux are also provided for download.

papers.title: Probing radial flow via the differential flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ using CMS open data
papers.summary: We present a comprehensive study of the differential radial flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ and its $p_T$-integrated counterpart $v_0$ in Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$, using CMS open data for mid-peripheral centrality classes of 50--60\% and 60--70\%. The measured $v_0(p_T)$ distributions are compared with ATLAS measurements at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, revealing a clear energy dependence in the overall magnitude of radial flow fluctuations. Notably, the scaled ratio $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ exhibits an approximate universality that is largely independent of both collision energy and centrality at low $p_T$, persisting up to $p_T\sim3~\mathrm{GeV}$, suggesting that the integrated $v_0$ encodes most of the energy-dependent information. We compare the data with the \textsc{Jetscape} multi-stage hybrid model, using Gaussian process emulators trained on a principal component analysis of the model output to explore the full 17-dimensional parameter space. A global variance-based sensitivity analysis using Sobol indices shows that, for the Grad viscous correction, the nucleon fluctuation parameter $σ_k$ is the dominant source of variance for $v_0$, $v_0(p_T)$, and $v_0(p_T)/v_0$, followed by the free-streaming parameters $τ_R$ and $α$ and the nucleon width $w$. The sensitivity to the bulk viscosity peak $(ζ/s)_{\max}$ is weak for $v_0$ but increases for $v_0(p_T)$ and for the scaled ratio. Emulator predictions, calibrated on $p_T$-integrated observables and on scaled spectra, describe the data reasonably well at low and intermediate $p_T$. Parameters calibrated at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$ also describe the ATLAS $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ data at $5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, supporting a near universal momentum dependence of radial flow fluctuations across collision energies.

papers.title: Critical step size of stochastic gradient descent for a linear neuron: an exact solution and the role of the input spectrum
papers.summary: We study online stochastic gradient descent for a single linear neuron in a teacher-student setting with Gaussian inputs of arbitrary covariance. The mean-square errors of the $N$ weights obey a closed linear recursion of dimension $N$, which we solve exactly. We prove that the dynamics converges if and only if the step size is below a critical value $λ_c$, given by an explicit scalar equation that involves all the eigenvalues of the input covariance, and we obtain the stationary error of each weight, which diverges at $λ_c$. This condition coincides with the classical mean-square stability condition of the least-mean-squares filter; our derivation is elementary and self-contained. We then show that $λ_c$ is controlled by the effective rank $Ω_1$ of the input covariance rather than by the number of parameters, $1/(Ω_1+2) \leq λ_c < 1/Ω_1$ in rescaled units: the critical step size is inversely proportional to $N$ only for isotropic inputs, whereas it decays more slowly, or saturates, for power-law spectra. Finally, we extend the solution to mini-batches of size $B$: the critical step size grows linearly with $B$ and saturates once $B$ exceeds the effective rank.

papers.title: Cleaning correlation matrices with external information: the Maximum Variance estimat
papers.summary: Rotationally invariant estimators clean the eigenvalues of an empirical correlation matrix but keep its noisy eigenvectors. We study an estimator that corrects the eigenvectors by using external information, namely a partition of the assets into groups such as asset classes or regions. The Maximum Variance (MaxVar) estimator restricts the leading eigenvectors to linear combinations of the maximum-variance portfolios of the groups and replaces the rest of the spectrum by a single eigenvalue. It is a factor model with about n parameters instead of n2/2, and it is positive de nite even when the number of observations is smaller than the number of assets n. We apply it to the correlation matrix of 47 futures on stock indices, bonds and currencies, with the three asset classes as groups. In an illustrative Monte Carlo test, in which the reference matrix has the structure assumed by the estimator, the distance to the reference is reduced by one third with respect to the empirical matrix, against less than 10% for the rotationally invariant estimator. The decisive test is the performance of a portfolio on real data: over 1993-2018, the Sharpe ratio of the risk parity portfolio, which involves the inverse of the matrix, is 1.28 with the MaxVar estimator, 1.24 with the rotationally invariant estimator and 1.17 with the empirical matrix, and the advantage increases when the estimation window is shortened.

papers.title: Turbulent Epidemics: Scale-dependent Fluctuations as a Probe of Population Heterogeneity
papers.summary: Heterogeneous dynamics, including phenomena such as superspreading and clustering, is a hallmark of many infectious diseases. A key challenge lies in identifying observables that constrain heterogeneous dynamics. We here adapt the technique of turbulence decomposition from fluid dynamics to extract scale-dependent fluctuation spectra and correlation functions from disaggregated epidemiological data as a probe of population heterogeneity. To investigate possible explanations for the observed heterogeneities during the COVID-19 winter wave in Germany in 2020/21, we calculate synthetic observables using the new network-based simulation code \textsc{Epimetheus} for an idealized structured population. The code can flexibly incorporate clustering, heterogeneous connectivity and susceptibility, superspreading as well as temporal modulations of transmission risk and factors like waning of immunity and vaccination. A qualitative comparison of simulated and observed fluctuation spectra and correlation functions as well as the secondary attack rate and the overdispersion indicates that both clustering and variations of susceptibility across population substructures of all scales are required to produce the observed dynamics. Combined with heterogeneous connectivity, it is likely that self-limiting effects would have limited the winter outbreak to $0.2\texttt{-}0.35$ of the population without further behavioral changes after the autumn of 2020. A uniform population-wide reduction of transmission risk alone does not adequately explain the observed heterogeneities. Further analysis of the relative contributions and interplay of interventions and self-limiting effects on COVID-19 disease dynamics is required. We outline avenues towards a better integration of heterogeneity in models for predicting infectious disease dynamics and diagnosing effects of interventions.

papers.title: 1+1 dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration
papers.summary: We study $(1+1)$-dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration under the conformal equation of state $\varepsilon=3p$. We evolve temperature, fluid rapidity, and shear stress using energy conservation, longitudinal momentum conservation, and a shear-relaxation law in a prescribed transverse magnetic stress. Moving beyond longitudinal boost invariance, we derive perturbative analytical expressions in the Navier--Stokes approximation and obtain nonlinear solutions with shear relaxation, comparing dynamical and prescribed accelerating flows from identical initial conditions. The initial temperature curvature generates a longitudinal pressure gradient that alters the rapidity slope, modifies longitudinal expansion work, and produces a distinct cooling history. For the reference parameters, shear viscosity enhances the resulting central temperature difference much more strongly than the prescribed magnetic stress, while the condition for equal central temperatures shifts with proper time and initial shear. At $χ=λ^*=0.03$, the maximum relative difference in central temperature is $0.18\%$ over $0.6$--$6$~fm/$c$, despite a persistent momentum residual in the prescribed flow. Because the velocity mapping also enters the entropy per unit fluid rapidity, the rapidity distribution remains sensitive to the flow evolution even when central temperatures closely agree. Replacing the prescribed field with ideal induction removes direct magnetic work while retaining magnetic pressure and inertia in the longitudinal momentum balance.

papers.title: How Systems Treat Intent: A Faceted Taxonomy of Intent for Human-AI Co-Creation
papers.summary: Human-AI interaction depends on systems acting on user intent rather than explicit procedures, even when that intent is incomplete, evolving, or partially communicable. Literature organizing systems by interaction technique, workflow stage, or division of labor, offer limited insight into which facet of intent an interaction mechanism addresses. We introduce a six-facet taxonomy of intent, grounded in philosophical accounts of mind, action, and meaning, and apply it to systems presented in 198 papers from eleven SIGCHI venues. Our analysis reveals that different forms of incomplete intent are associated with distinct interaction and authorship strategies, showing that mechanisms that appear similar often address fundamentally different intent-related problems. This exposes blind spots, as intent is rarely represented as an interaction object, authorship provenance is rarely tracked, and tentative preferences are rarely distinguished from firm commitments. The taxonomy offers a lens for analyzing and designing AI systems around the facets of intent they address.

papers.title: From joint attention to shared symbols: A free-energy principle account
papers.summary: Joint attention precedes vocabulary acquisition. How can attending to the same object help two people with different sensory experiences come to use a shared word? In a free-energy principle account, marginalizing the common object induces a statistical dependence between private perceptual states. In a categorical world, the joint prior inherits a mixture structure whose component index provides a candidate for shared reference. The collective predictive coding model approximates this prior by representing the dependence through that shared index. An established Metropolis-Hastings naming game lets agents infer and exchange words using private evidence. Toy and multiview image experiments illustrate how word exchange can coordinate private categories and improve the fit of collective models. The account connects joint attention to shared symbols through the coupling of private inference.

papers.title: A general formalism for electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon
papers.summary: We develop a general formalism for the electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon, $γ_{\rm v}N\toΦ_1Φ_2B$, that can be used in single-channel as well as coupled-channel analyses over a wide range of energies. In the spirit of the decomposition introduced by Berends et al. for single-meson electroproduction, the hadronic current is expanded in a set of 16 gauge- and Lorentz-invariant matrices, four of which vanish for real photons. The corresponding Lorentz-invariant (Dirac) amplitudes can be obtained from any reaction model and are mapped onto 16 CGLN-like Pauli amplitudes, from which the five-fold differential cross section and its transverse, longitudinal, and interference response functions follow directly. Although these matrices are not all linearly independent, they follow directly from the covariant decomposition of the current, so the amplitudes can be read off from the Feynman diagrams and the observables take a simpler, more symmetric form. As a first application, we calculate the $γp\toπ^0π^0p$ and $γp\toπ^+π^0n$ reactions near threshold from tree-level nucleon Born terms. This example shows explicitly how the Dirac amplitudes are read off from Feynman diagrams and how gauge invariance, which is violated by the individual diagrams, is restored in the total amplitude and preserved when hadronic form factors are included. The formalism thus provides a versatile basis for future theoretical and phenomenological studies of double-meson photo- and electroproduction. A more complete abstract is provided in the paper.

papers.title: Comparison of 3D-DXA Measurements with QCT Software Solutions for Proximal Femur Bone Density Assessment
papers.summary: 3D-Shaper reconstructs proximal femur shape and density in 3D from a standard hip dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scan. In men and women aged 35-91 years, we compared 3D-Shaper integral volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), trabecular vBMD, and cortical surface BMD (sBMD) with quantitative computed tomography (QCT) processed with three methods: an in-house pipeline, Stradview and QCTPro CTXA, which were used to derive bone measurements equivalent to those of 3D-Shaper. Agreement, including among QCT methods, was assessed with linear regression and Bland-Altman analysis (bias and limits of agreement, LoA). 3D-Shaper agreed strongly with the in-house pipeline and Stradview for integral vBMD (R=0.95-0.96; bias 1.5 to 4.2 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$39.7 to 41.4 mg/cm$^3$), trabecular vBMD (R=0.92-0.94; bias -11.8 to -7.8 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$33.3 to 39.4 mg/cm$^3$) and cortical sBMD (R=0.94; bias 5.6 to 38.2 mg/cm$^2$; LoA $\pm$23.6 to 26.4 mg/cm$^2$). The in-house pipeline and Stradview agreed for integral vBMD (R=1.00; bias -2.7 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$3.7 mg/cm$^3$), trabecular vBMD (R=0.96-1.00; bias -0.2 to 3.9 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$6.9 to 27.5 mg/cm$^3$) and cortical sBMD (R=0.98; bias 32.7 mg/cm$^2$; LoA $\pm$14.6 mg/cm$^2$). Compared with 3D-Shaper, QCTPro CTXA integral vBMD was systematically lower (R=0.90; bias -28.4 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$61.5 mg/cm$^3$) and trabecular vBMD showed a proportional bias (R=0.89; bias -44.1 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$61.3 mg/cm$^3$). The same pattern was observed against the other QCT methods, for integral vBMD (R=0.93; bias -32.6 to -29.9 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$49.6 to 50.0 mg/cm$^3$) and trabecular vBMD (R=0.94-0.96; bias -36.3 to -32.5 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$51.2 to 54.9 mg/cm$^3$). These findings support the agreement of 3D-Shaper with independent QCT approaches and show that 3D-Shaper-QCT differences must be interpreted in light of the QCT method used.

papers.title: CCFinance: Reconstructing Financial News Samples from Web Archives
papers.summary: Proprietary news archives assign stories to firms, so reproducing a financial study often requires access to both the articles and the vendor's assignments. CCFinance lets researchers reconstruct firm coverage under different selection rules by recording which version of a story was captured, which issuers it names and how often each appears. From 14.8 million English-language records in Fine News, derived from public Common Crawl News, we identify 5.22 million distinct, consistently dated articles with issuer links. Exact reconstruction requires the restricted snapshot and derived artifacts. We compare GLiNER and Stanza on 250 model-labeled article leads and assess issuer links and story focus against blinded model judgments. Estimated precision among 475 accepted links is 96.8%. Among held-out articles with a detected company, requiring three mentions raises subject precision from 31.9% to 66.1%. Across the 2017-2025 panel, the same rule reduces the number of issuer-years with at least 50 qualifying stories from 13,918 to 8,641. Three reimplementations examine volatility tracking, bank networks and overnight returns. In the network study, bank pairs appearing together rose from 177 to 242 across publishers between January and April 2020, but fell from 50 to 35 within Reuters.

papers.title: The Private Production of Safety Outside Options and the Burden of Protection
papers.summary: Protective interventions are typically evaluated by their ability to prevent harm. Yet protection also raises a distinct question: who bears the burden of adjusting to violence? I examine this allocation of protective adjustment using four randomized interventions in the United States. An offer of permanent housing assistance increases separation from a baseline partner combined with stable independent housing by 12.52 percentage points. Assignment to active police-response protocols reduces observed victim-only departures and increases suspect-only departures. Assignment to an emergency protection order increases documented directions for suspects to leave. These findings reveal two margins of the same allocation problem: housing assistance expands victims' ability to establish an independent residence, while enforcement shifts displacement obligations toward suspects. Protective policies thus shape not only the opportunities for safety, but also the distribution of the costs required to achieve it.

papers.title: Hint of universality in $α$-cluster nuclei
papers.summary: The empirical ground-state energies of the $α$-cluster nuclei are placed on the universal function that governs $N$-boson systems with a shallow state. The data fall on the finite-range-corrected universal curve, suggesting Efimov-type universality. No excited states, transition strengths, radii, or cluster geometries enter the analysis; the nuclei are treated as $N$ structureless bosons. A zero-shape $α$-$α$ Bargmann potential, describing the $^{8}$Be resonance, provides the pairwise interaction with no shape freedom. Simple three- and four-body forces, each a single Gaussian in the hyperradius, are fitted to $^{12}$C and $^{16}$O; microscopic calculations for $^{20}$Ne and $^{24}$Mg ($N=5,6$) follow as parameter-free predictions. A compact $0^+_2$ state near the Hoyle energy emerges in $^{12}$C without being targeted by the fit.

papers.title: Construction of a conserved energy-momentum tensor of the Skyrmion coupled to additional dynamical degrees in the large-$N_c$ expansion
papers.summary: We formulate an order-by-order construction of a conserved energy-momentum tensor (EMT) in the large-$N_c$ expansion of the model where the Skyrmion is coupled to additional dynamical fields. We show that, expanding the equations of motion and the EMT in powers of $1/N_c$, the inclusion of the backreaction to the Skyrmion from the additional fields is essential for achieving the conservation law of the EMT, which is contrasted with the fixed-background approximation where the effects of backreaction are neglected. We apply the construction to the model for hyperons based on the Callan-Klebanov bound-state approach, where the antikaon is bound to the Skyrmion, to obtain the EMT up to next-to-leading order of the $1/N_c$ expansion. We explicitly show that the divergence of the EMT from the backreaction for the Skyrmion exactly cancels that of the kaon to achieve the conservation of the total EMT. We find that the conserved EMT gives a negative hyperon D-term whose magnitude is smaller than that of the nucleon D-term and radii of gravitational form factors for the hyperon smaller than those for the nucleon, which implies that the hyperon is more compact than the nucleon.

papers.title: The user who is not there: genealogy and critique of simulated users built with generative AI in UX testing
papers.summary: Usability testing depends on people, and people's time does not speed up at the pace that software production demands. Large language models (LLMs) now promise to remove people from testing by generating simulated users that browse websites, answer questionnaires and give interviews. This paper examines how academic research understands that promise. It combines a critical literature review with a genealogical reading that follows the simulated user from the cognitive models of the 1980s to current generative agents. The paper makes four claims. First, testing without the user is an old aim of human-computer interaction (HCI), and cost has always justified it. Second, the validity criterion for user models shifted from predictive precision to believability, and recent studies that return to precision report weak results. Third, simulated participants conflict with the values of academic research and with methods that treat participation as a political right, with Participatory Design as the limit case. Fourth, the Latin American literature found in this review uses generative AI to support expert inspection and contains no study of synthetic users. That gap leaves open questions about who gets represented and about research ethics regulation in Brazil. The paper closes with an agenda of open problems. As part of its method, it reports that the review itself used an LLM as research assistant, and it discusses what that implies.

papers.title: Learning Multimodal Representations from Partially Paired, Small-Scale Data
papers.summary: Modeling multimodal data from partially paired samples is critical for advancing domains like biomedicine, where vast unimodal datasets and foundation models exist but paired data remains scarce. Existing fusion methods rely on large-scale paired datasets, limiting their use in scenarios with incomplete pairing. We introduce CAMEO, an adversarial learning-based modality fusion framework that integrates modalities from small, partially paired datasets. Combining any pre-trained unimodal encoder with a cross-modal latent alignment mechanism, CAMEO learns shared representations requiring only minimal paired samples. Evaluated on computational pathology tasks such as niche classification and cell type composition prediction, CAMEO achieves superior data efficiency, outperforming contrastive approaches like CLIP in low paired-data regimes, and highlighting the benefits of adversarial alignment when paired annotations are scarce. To facilitate further research, we additionally release a fully annotated HuggingFace dataset comprising three organs and paired image and gene expression modalities. By extending fusion methods to address limited pairing and small-scale datasets, we provide a framework that advances multimodal learning and broadens its applicability to real-world biomedical problems.

papers.title: An Experimental Apparatus for Embodied Conversational AI: A Simple Implementation Coupling a Commercial Voice AI with an Avatar
papers.summary: As generative AI becomes integrated into everyday life, understanding how avatars shape human-AI interaction and the perception of AI as a social partner is becoming increasingly important. This paper builds a research instrument on audio-output coupling, which connects the audio output of a generative AI to an external avatar. There are two implementations: the browser implementation captures the audio of a tab selected through screen sharing without installing additional software, and the desktop implementation captures the audio of the service embedded in the application. Both work with the voice AI as people ordinarily use it, and as a method neither depends on a particular service. The implementation reported here, Deskmate, generates speech state, mouth shape, and expression from low-level features such as voice-band mean amplitude, RMS, peak, and transients. Because it uses no microphone, speech recognition, or transcription, Deskmate acquires neither the user's voice nor the content of the conversation. Records of the conversation remain with the voice AI provider, but none are kept automatically on the side of Deskmate. Three interchangeable backends are provided for rendering the avatar: 3D (VRM), 2D (Live2D), and CSS. Deskmate allows researchers to manipulate avatar presentation as an experimental condition, without changing the commercial service's interface, voice, or response generation. Because conversation content is not held fixed, the estimand is the total effect, including the changes in the participant's speech and the AI's responses that the presentation brings about. A server edition, served from the researcher's server for online experiments, is also provided. The effectiveness of avatar presentation has not yet been evaluated; this paper reports the design and implementation.

papers.title: Beyond the Blueprint: The Continuing Evolution of Turing's Theory of Morphogenesis
papers.summary: Turing's article ``The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis'' has profoundly influenced conceptual views on the emergence of biological form across scales and species. It has also served as a foundational framework to guide experimental investigations into the mechanisms that underlie pattern formation. In this article, we trace the historical development of Turing's ideas and examine their integration into contemporary research programs. We critically assess the broad and often overlapping concepts that have derived from Turing's work, both highlighting value in productive applications of the theory and suggesting that skepticism should remain in overly simplistic validations. By clarifying these concepts and their intrinsic limitations, we rethink contemporary approaches aimed at understanding the essential principles that govern biological pattern formation. We pose some important challenges that will require interdisciplinary expertise to overcome, and which will necessitate fundamentally new paradigms to understand the physical origin of Darwin's ``endless forms most beautiful''.

papers.title: Chiral crossover responses in a magnetic field: Finite-$μ_5$ matching in the NJL model
papers.summary: We investigate how independent information at finite chiral chemical potential $μ_5$ constrains pseudocritical-temperature responses in the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model under a magnetic field. Vacuum calibration alone leaves the coefficient $c_r$ of the additional interaction $δΩ_r=c_rμ_5^2(M-m_0)^2$ undetermined. We compare soft-cutoff (SC) and Pauli-Villars (PV) vacuum regularizations, each combined with the direct treatment (D) or the magnetic finite-difference scheme (MFDS). The reference SC and PV treatments exhibit opposite finite-$μ_5$ responses already at $eB=0$. Matching the $eB=0$ scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio predicted by unitarized chiral perturbation theory gives $c_{\mathrm{SC}}=-0.07112$ and $c_{\mathrm{PV}}=0.22479$. Holding these coefficients fixed at $eB=0.1,0.2,0.4$ GeV$^2$ reduces the four-treatment spread of the normalized finite-$μ_5$-induced mass-inflection temperature change by factors of approximately $7.5$-$15.3$ at $μ_5=0.15$ GeV and $18.1$-$32.6$ at $μ_5=0.30$ GeV. For the distinct scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio at $μ_5=0.15$ GeV, the spread decreases by factors of approximately $74$, $27$, and $14$ at the same magnetic fields, respectively. The reduction in regularization-dependent finite-$μ_5$ responses thus persists at the sampled nonzero magnetic fields without further matching.

papers.title: Pesticide mixtures may compromise ecosystem services provided by an egg parasitoid of soybean pest stink bugs: a comprehensive ecotoxicological risk assessment
papers.summary: Tank mixtures of crop protection products are widely used in agricultural systems, yet their integrated effects on biological control agents remain poorly understood. We evaluated the lethal, sublethal, and transgenerational effects of four synthetic insecticides, applied alone or in binary mixtures with three fungicides and two herbicides, on adults and pupae of Telenomus podisi (Hymenoptera: Scelionidae), an important egg parasitoid of pest stink bugs. In adult bioassays, LC50 values ranged from 28.26 mg a.i. L-1 for isocycloseram + lambda-cyhalothrin to 265.88 mg a.i. L-1 for acephate. Overall, mixtures increased adverse effects relative to the individual products, reducing survival, parasitism, and longevity. The lowest parasitism rates occurred with isocycloseram + lambda-cyhalothrin combined with chlorothalonil or glyphosate SL formulation. Transgenerational effects were also detected, including reduced F1 emergence and an increased proportion of males in some treatments. Following pupal exposure, several mixtures reduced F0 emergence, whereas ethiprole + fenpropimorph and acephate + bixafen + prothioconazole + trifloxystrobin also reduced parasitism and longevity of the emerged adults. Integration of lethal and sublethal responses using the reduction coefficient (Ex) revealed increased toxicity for several mixtures and shifts in IOBC risk classification; notably, all insecticide + glyphosate mixtures reached Ex = 100% after pupal exposure. These findings show that assessing pesticides individually may underestimate ecotoxicological risk to T. podisi and highlight the need to consider pesticide mixtures in integrated pest management programs.

papers.title: Tidal effects of bulk viscosity in neutron stars
papers.summary: Bulk viscosity in neutron-star matter provides a temperature-dependent mechanism for tidal dissipation. In this study, we investigate the impact of bulk viscosity on the dissipative tidal response of neutron stars composed of neutrons, protons, and electrons. Employing cold equations of state derived through the momentum-dependent interaction model, we examine the bulk viscosity arising from the direct Urca process, which acts to restore chemical equilibrium. The temperature dependence is incorporated through the weak-interaction rate, allowing us to explore the behavior of bulk viscosity in the neutrino-transparent regime at temperatures up to a few MeV. To account for the spatial distribution of bulk viscosity within neutron stars, we introduce the effective bulk viscosity, a volume-averaged quantity over the region where direct Urca process operates, and establish a connection with the bulk viscosity. Specifically, we investigate its implications for tidal quantities, including the lag time and dissipative deformability, highlighting their dependence on temperature and stellar compactness. We find that the dissipative tidal effects become maximal at a temperature approximately coinciding with the one of maximum bulk viscosity on the onset of direct Urca. Additionally, these effects are more pronounced in intermediate neutron star masses compared to maximum ones. Finally, for both canonical $1.4\;M_\odot$ and maximum-mass neutron star configurations, we derive causality-based upper bounds on these quantities, providing theoretical benchmarks for assessing the potential observability of bulk-viscous effects in gravitational-wave signals from binary neutron star inspirals.

papers.title: Bypassing the Nanoampere Limit: A Thick-Target Methodology for Ultra-Low-Energy Resonances in the $^{11}$B(p,$α$)2$α$ Reaction
papers.summary: Precise measurements of the low-energy cross section for the $^{11}$B(p,$α$)2$α$ reaction is critical for nuclear astrophysics and fusion energy research, yet such measurements are experimentally demanding due to the reaction's extremely small cross section. Conventional thin-target experiments are fundamentally limited to nanoampere beam currents, which restrict count rates to impractical levels at ultra-low proton energies. To overcome this limitation, we report a correction-free thick-target methodology capable of operating at beam currents of 20-60 microamperes, corresponding to a gain of over three orders of magnitude. Monte Carlo simulations of the full reaction kinematics are employed to determine the absolute reaction yield, eliminating the requirement for empirical normalization factors. At the well-known 148~keV (c.m.) resonance peak, our extracted resonance energy ($E_{\mathrm{r}} = 148.0$~keV) and level width ($Γ_{\mathrm{cm}} = 5.3$~keV) are demonstrated in good agreement with published data. A scheme via comparing the measured reaction probability with a theoretical extrapolation result is furtherly presented to probe low-energy resonances below 100~keV region. Preliminary measurements at proton energies of 75~keV and 100~keV reveal no evidence for additional low-energy resonances. This work provides a robust new methodology to measure cross section and resonance parameters for the p$^{11}$B reaction and offers a highly efficient tool for systematic resonance searches in the ultra-low-energy regime.

papers.title: Effect of dark matter and scalar-cut potential on the macroscopic properties of neutron stars: A chiral quark mean field approach
papers.summary: We investigate the effects of fermionic dark matter (DM) and scalar-cut potential ($U_{\text{cut}}(φ)$) on the equation of state (EOS) and macroscopic properties of neutron stars. The baryonic matter consists of neutrons, protons, electrons, and muons under the $β$-equilibrium and is described within the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model. In this framework, quarks are confined within baryons, whose properties are modified through the exchange of scalar fields $σ$, $ζ$, and $δ$, and vector fields $ω$ and $ρ$. The DM is modelled as a self-interacting fermionic fluid with scalar $\varphi_D$ and vector $V_D^μ$ mediators. The baryonic and DM fluids interact only through gravity and are treated within a two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff formalism. We examine the resulting mass-radius relation and tidal deformability, along with the gravitational redshift, to investigate the effects of DM on neutron star structure and observable properties. The inclusion of $U_{\text{cut}}(φ)$ stiffens the EOS, whereas increasing the DM fraction generally softens the EOS and modifies the mass-radius relation, tidal deformability, and gravitational redshift. The magnitude and nature of these modifications depend on the DM particle mass and mediator interactions, which determine whether the resulting configurations exhibit compact DM cores or extended DM halos.

papers.title: Revealing Nuclear Shape through Identified-Hadron Flow Decorrelations
papers.summary: Relativistic nuclear collisions encode nuclear shape in collective flow, yet the potential of identified hadrons to disentangle deformation modes remains largely unexplored. Using event-by-event viscous hydrodynamics coupled to hadronic transport, we investigate momentum-dependent elliptic-flow decorrelations of pions, kaons, and protons in central $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U collisions at 193 GeV and $^{20}$Ne+$^{20}$Ne collisions at 5.36 TeV. The identified species exhibit distinct momentum- and deformation-dependent responses, with nuclear-shape information persisting in their relative correlations even when individual deformation effects are weak. We introduce crossing coordinates $(P_{\rm cross},R_{\rm cross})$, defined by the intersection of pion-kaon and pion-proton flow-factorization ratios. Variations of quadrupole deformation and triaxiality generate distinct trajectories in the crossing plane, offering complementary constraints on both nuclear-shape parameters. The corresponding behavior persists in higher-moment correlations, while an energy comparison in Ne+Ne reveals the influence of collision dynamics. Our findings establish identified-particle flow decorrelations as a complementary approach to probing and constraining intrinsic nuclear geometry.

papers.title: Causal Evidence for the Emergence and Spread of Reward Hacking in AI Agent Swarms
papers.summary: Autonomous AI agents that coordinate and collaborate among each other have become pervasive across domains ranging from scientific research to finance and engineering. The opportunity to share messages and build upon each other's work also creates the potential for misaligned behaviors to spread across AI agents. We provide causal evidence that mere exposure to reward hacking, cheating on a task to pass an automated check, is enough to spread the behavior among AI agents, even after the cheat has been rejected. We conducted 17 preregistered experiments with six frontier models (n = 20,111 agents). First, we show that cheating emerges spontaneously. When agents were told that work passing the visible tests is accepted, 33% cheated in the first round, when the shared record of teammates' submissions was empty. Second, we show that agents who rarely cheat when working alone cheat most of the time after seeing a teammate's cheat, as 94% of teammates who saw an accepted cheat cheated. Third, we show that rejection of reward-hacked solutions offers little protection, using experiments that changed only the label on the cheat. Most agents copied a cheat labeled rejected, 34% of agents cheated after an AI reviewer had rejected the cheat, and nearly every agent copied a cheat labeled accepted. Fourth, we show that cheating generalizes to new tasks. On a new problem with an empty collaboration record, 70% of agents who had earlier seen an accepted cheat cheated again, compared with 32% of agents who had seen an empty record. Fifth, we show that cheating spreads from neighbor to neighbor through networks of 256 agents. In the networks, 44% of agents with a cheating neighbor cheated, compared with 2% of other agents. Together, the results suggest that mere exposure can spread misaligned behavior among AI agents, and that catching a cheat is insufficient once other agents have seen the cheat.

papers.title: MindBridge: A Multilingual and Multimodal Tool for Interactive Cognitive Monitoring
papers.summary: We present MindBridge, a clinician-informed, multilingual, multimodal cognitive monitoring tool combining participant-controlled interviews with explainable reports. Reports link lexical diversity and pause patterns to speech or text evidence and disclose data quality and missingness. In a formative study of typed interaction with 10 adults (seven aged 18-59; three aged 60 or older), follow-ups prompted elaboration but sometimes introduced assumptions requiring correction. Nine participants ranked interpretation-first reports highest; all identified score-only reports as most likely to encourage fixation and overreaction. On a fixed DementiaBank manifest, the best configuration achieved 70.3% zero-shot accuracy on valid predictions versus a 56.0% majority-class baseline on the full manifest. Some configurations predicted only one category; tests with generated samples revealed different error patterns across input types and languages. MindBridge makes evidence collection, analysis, and interpretation inspectable, linking participant control to the scope and limits of monitoring results.

papers.title: Managing Uncertainty in Teacher Vibe Coding: A Comparison of Teacher and Expert Workflows
papers.summary: Vibe coding, or natural language software development, enables teachers to become creators of digital teaching artifacts. However, novice educators oftentimes face different barriers. This qualitative study examined the workflows of pre-service teachers, in-service teachers, and expert developers through think-aloud protocols. Findings reveal vibe coding operates through a loop of problem framing, development, and verification governed by uncertainty management. Teachers reduced uncertainty by grounding designs in authentic needs: pre-service teachers drew on pedagogical principles, whereas in-service teachers relied on everyday teaching challenges. Conversely, Experts reduced ambiguity by constraining requirements, decomposing artifacts into testable modules, and automating tests. These differences reveal complementary forms of pedagogical, contextual, and technical expertise. Future work may be about supporting nontechnical teachers in developing reliable and educational applications.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Accepted for presentation at the 2027 American Educational Research Association Annual Meeting

papers.title: But Can You Draw It Live? The Emergence of AI Duidus for Adjudicating Suspected Generative AI Use in Digital Art Commission Communities
papers.summary: Generative AI poses new challenges for digital art commission communities, where a commission's value often depends on human labor and authorship. We examine a novel community-developed dispute resolution mechanism called an AI duidu, or livestreamed drawing bet, used when an artist is suspected of using generative AI. In an AI duidu, an accuser challenges an artist to create a new artwork live, and community members vote on whether the artist created the disputed artwork without AI assistance. Often, both parties stake money with an intermediary, who releases it after the vote. Through interviews with 17 accusers, accused artists, or intermediaries, we examined how the AI duidu emerged and how participants perceived its effectiveness and risks. We found that AI duidus shift authorship verification from the artwork itself to the artist, using livestreamed creative labor, community adjudication, and wagering to establish provenance and negotiate community norms surrounding AI use.
